column3: A polite way to address a woman about your mother's age, even a stranger: 阿姨，请问…. Children use it for their mother's friends, and 阿姨 is also the real "maternal aunt" and, in a city household, a hired helper or nanny. The 阿 in front of a kinship term makes it affectionate and spoken.
column4: 阿姨，请问洗手间在哪儿？
column5: 阿姨，請問洗手間在哪兒？
column6: Āyí, qǐngwèn xǐshǒujiān zài nǎr?
column7: Excuse me, auntie, where is the restroom?
column9: A polite way to address a woman about your mother's age, even a stranger: 阿姨，請問…. Children use it for their mother's friends, and 阿姨 is also the real "maternal aunt" and, in a city household, a hired helper or nanny. The 阿 in front of a kinship term makes it affectionate and spoken.

column3: Your father's younger brother, and the word children use for any man about their father's age: 叔叔好 is the standard greeting. Written with the same character twice, with the second one in the neutral tone. 叔叔 is for an uncle on the father's side only; the mother's brother is 舅舅.
column6: Háizimen jiào tā shūshu.
column7: The children call him uncle.
column9: Your father's younger brother, and the word children use for any man about their father's age: 叔叔好 is the standard greeting. Written with the same character twice, with the second one in the neutral tone. 叔叔 is for an uncle on the father's side only; the mother's brother is 舅舅.

column3: Big brother, the eldest brother in a family, and a respectful address for a man of about your age or somewhat older, especially to a stranger or in a shop: 大哥，谢谢你. It can also mean the boss of a gang. 哥 is 可 written twice, one above the other.
column6: Dàgē, xièxie nǐ bāngmáng.
column7: Brother, thanks for your help.
column9: Big brother, the eldest brother in a family, and a respectful address for a man of about your age or somewhat older, especially to a stranger or in a shop: 大哥，謝謝你. It can also mean the boss of a gang. 哥 is 可 written twice, one above the other.

column3: Eldest sister, and a friendly address for a woman a little older than you, used with strangers: 大姐，这个多少钱？ It is warmer and more informal than 女士. The 姐 has 女 for the meaning and 且 for the sound.
column6: Dàjiě, zhège duōshao qián?
column7: Ma'am, how much is this?
column9: Eldest sister, and a friendly address for a woman a little older than you, used with strangers: 大姐，這個多少錢？ It is warmer and more informal than 女士. The 姐 has 女 for the meaning and 且 for the sound.

column3: A respectful address for a woman of your mother's age or older, much used with neighbors and market sellers: 大妈，早上好. Strictly it is also your father's elder brother's wife. It feels older than 阿姨, which suits a woman who is a little younger.
column6: Dàmā zài gōngyuán lǐ tiàowǔ.
column7: An older woman is dancing in the park.
column9: A respectful address for a woman of your mother's age or older, much used with neighbors and market sellers: 大媽，早上好. Strictly it is also your father's elder brother's wife. It feels older than 阿姨, which suits a woman who is a little younger.

column3: A respectful address for an elderly man, a stranger or a neighbor: 大爷，您慢走. It can also mean your father's elder brother. Say it with 您 to be polite. The 爷 is neutral, so dàye.
column6: Dàye zuò zài shù xià xià qí.
column7: An old man is sitting under a tree playing chess.
column9: A respectful address for an elderly man, a stranger or a neighbor: 大爺，您慢走. It can also mean your father's elder brother. Say it with 您 to be polite. The 爺 is neutral, so dàye.

column3: Husband, the spoken, affectionate word, used by wives of their own husband: 我老公. It is not for written or formal use; there 丈夫 is the word. 老 is "old" here only in the sense of familiar, the same 老 as in 老师.
column6: Wǒ lǎogong jīntiān jiābān.
column7: My husband is working overtime today.
column9: Husband, the spoken, affectionate word, used by wives of their own husband: 我老公. It is not for written or formal use; there 丈夫 is the word. 老 is "old" here only in the sense of familiar, the same 老 as in 老師.

column3: Wife, the spoken, affectionate word, used by husbands of their own wife: 我老婆. Paired with 老公. In writing and formal speech use 妻子. It is not for someone else's wife in polite talk.
column6: Wǒ lǎopo zuòfàn hěn hǎochī.
column7: My wife's cooking is delicious.
column9: Wife, the spoken, affectionate word, used by husbands of their own wife: 我老婆. Paired with 老公. In writing and formal speech use 妻子. It is not for someone else's wife in polite talk.

column3: Wife, the neutral standard word that works in speech and writing: 他的妻子. Its pair is 丈夫. The 子 here is just a light suffix and is neutral. In casual talk married people say 老婆 instead.
column6: Tā de qīzi shì yī wèi yīshēng.
column7: His wife is a doctor.
column9: Wife, the neutral standard word that works in speech and writing: 他的妻子. Its pair is 丈夫. The 子 here is just a light suffix and is neutral. In casual talk married people say 老婆 instead.

column3: Husband, the standard word in speech and writing: 她的丈夫. Its pair is 妻子. The 夫 is neutral (zhàngfu). 丈 on its own is an old unit of length, about 3 meters.
column6: Tā de zhàngfu zài yínháng gōngzuò.
column7: Her husband works at a bank.
column9: Husband, the standard word in speech and writing: 她的丈夫. Its pair is 妻子. The 夫 is neutral (zhàngfu). 丈 on its own is an old unit of length, about 3 meters.

column3: Husband and wife, a married couple, in speech as well as in writing: 夫妻两个人, 一对夫妻 ("a married couple"). 夫 is the man and 妻 the wife. A common set phrase is 老夫老妻, an old married couple.
column4: 他们是一对幸福的夫妻。
column5: 他們是一對幸福的夫妻。
column6: Tāmen shì yī duì xìngfú de fūqī.
column7: They are a happy married couple.
column9: Husband and wife, a married couple, in speech as well as in writing: 夫妻兩個人, 一對夫妻 ("a married couple"). 夫 is the man and 妻 the wife. A common set phrase is 老夫老妻, an old married couple.

column3: Married couple, a little more formal or written than 夫妻, and usually used about someone else: 年轻夫妇 "a young couple", 这对夫妇. You count them with 对 as with 夫妻. 夫 is the husband and 妇 the woman (a married woman), so the two characters are the pair.
column6: Zhè duì fūfù yǒu liǎng ge háizi.
column7: This couple has two children.
column9: Married couple, a little more formal or written than 夫妻, and usually used about someone else: 年輕夫婦 "a young couple", 這對夫婦. You count them with 對 as with 夫妻. 夫 is the husband and 婦 the woman (a married woman), so the two characters are the pair.

column3: A polite word for the wife of someone of standing: 总统夫人 "the president's wife", 李夫人 "Mrs. Li". Use it for someone else's wife, never for your own, and it fits formal or written settings. Also used in "Madam": 夫人，请坐.
column6: Zǒngtǒng fūren cānjiā le huìyì.
column7: The president's wife attended the meeting.
column9: A polite word for the wife of someone of standing: 總統夫人 "the president's wife", 李夫人 "Mrs. Li". Use it for someone else's wife, never for your own, and it fits formal or written settings. Also used in "Madam": 夫人，請坐.

column3: Grandson on the son's side: your son's son. A daughter's children are 外孙. Add 女 and it becomes 孙女. The 子 is neutral: sūnzi.
column6: Yéye dài sūnzi qù gōngyuán.
column7: Grandpa takes his grandson to the park.
column9: Grandson on the son's side: your son's son. A daughter's children are 外孫. Add 女 and it becomes 孫女. The 子 is neutral: sūnzi.

column3: Granddaughter on the son's side: your son's daughter. The pair is 孙子, and a daughter's daughter is 外孙女. 孙 is built from 子 "child" and 小.
column6: Nǎinai zuì ài tā de sūnnǚ.
column7: Grandma loves her granddaughter most.
column9: Granddaughter on the son's side: your son's daughter. The pair is 孫子, and a daughter's daughter is 外孫女. 孫 is built from 子 "child" and 小.

column3: Sisters, also a group of sisters or a woman's close female friends: 姐妹们, 我的好姐妹. For counting, 两个姐妹 is fine, but "I have an older sister" is 我有一个姐姐. 姐 and 妹 both have 女 for the meaning and a sound part.
column6: Wǒ yǒu liǎng ge jiěmèi.
column7: I have two sisters.
column9: Sisters, also a group of sisters or a woman's close female friends: 姐妹們, 我的好姐妹. For counting, 兩個姐妹 is fine, but "I have an older sister" is 我有一個姐姐. 姐 and 妹 both have 女 for the meaning and a sound part.

column3: Brothers, the older and the younger together: 兄弟三个 "three brothers". Men also use it as a friendly address for a buddy: 兄弟，来喝一杯. Here 弟 is a full tone four, as opposed to the neutral 弟弟. 兄 shows a mouth 口 over a person 儿.
column4: 他们兄弟三个都喜欢踢足球。
column5: 他們兄弟三個都喜歡踢足球。
column6: Tāmen xiōngdì sān ge dōu xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
column7: The three brothers all like playing soccer.
column9: Brothers, the older and the younger together: 兄弟三個 "three brothers". Men also use it as a friendly address for a buddy: 兄弟，來喝一杯. Here 弟 is a full tone four, as opposed to the neutral 弟弟. 兄 shows a mouth 口 over a person 儿.

column3: A baby or small child, and a loving name for one: 宝宝乖, 小宝宝. It is a doubled 宝 "treasure", which is the picture of jade 玉 under a roof 宀. Parents may call a child of any age 宝宝, and partners use it too.
column6: Bǎobao jīntiān yī suì le.
column7: The baby is one year old today.
column9: A baby or small child, and a loving name for one: 寶寶乖, 小寶寶. It is a doubled 寶 "treasure", which is a roof 宀 over 珤 and 貝. Parents may call a child of any age 寶寶, and partners use it too.

column3: A "treasure", and a fond name for a child or a partner: 宝贝，该睡觉了. Both characters are about valuables, jade under a roof and a shell, which was once money. 宝贝 can also be used for a cherished object: 这是我的宝贝.
column6: Bǎobèi, gāi shuìjiào le.
column7: Darling, it's time to sleep.
column9: A "treasure", and a fond name for a child or a partner: 寶貝，該睡覺了. Both characters are about valuables, jade under a roof and a shell, which was once money. 寶貝 can also be used for a cherished object: 這是我的寶貝.

column3: Your "old home": the place your family comes from, such as the village or city of your parents, which may not be where you live now. 回老家 "go back to the family's hometown" is what many people do at Spring Festival. It differs from 家乡 by sounding more spoken and personal.
column6: Guònián wǒ yào huí lǎojiā.
column7: I'm going back to my hometown for New Year.
column9: Your "old home": the place your family comes from, such as the village or city of your parents, which may not be where you live now. 回老家 "go back to the family's hometown" is what many people do at Spring Festival. It differs from 家鄉 by sounding more spoken and personal.

column3: The "groom" at a wedding, paired with 新娘. 新 is "new" and 郎 an old word for a young man. It only describes the groom on his wedding day. The 良 in 郎 still sounds like it: láng and liáng.
column6: Xīnláng jīntiān hěn jǐnzhāng.
column7: The groom is very nervous today.
column9: The "groom" at a wedding, paired with 新娘. 新 is "new" and 郎 an old word for a young man. It only describes the groom on his wedding day. The 良 in 郎 still sounds like it: láng and liáng.

column3: The "bride", paired with 新郎. 娘 has 女 for the meaning and 良 for the sound, still close: niáng and liáng. On its own 娘 is an old word for "mother" and in some regions is still used so.
column6: Xīnniáng chuānzhe báisè de hūnshā.
column7: The bride is wearing a white wedding dress.
column9: The "bride", paired with 新郎. 娘 has 女 for the meaning and 良 for the sound, still close: niáng and liáng. On its own 娘 is an old word for "mother" and in some regions is still used so.

column3: A "wedding" as a ceremony: 婚 "marriage" plus 礼 "ceremony". Typical verbs are 参加婚礼 "attend a wedding", 举行婚礼 "hold a wedding". 婚 is built from 女 and 昏, which sounds alike. For the legal side, 结婚 is the word for getting married.
column4: 下个月我要参加朋友的婚礼。
column5: 下個月我要參加朋友的婚禮。
column6: Xià ge yuè wǒ yào cānjiā péngyou de hūnlǐ.
column7: Next month I'm going to a friend's wedding.
column9: A "wedding" as a ceremony: 婚 "marriage" plus 禮 "ceremony". Typical verbs are 參加婚禮 "attend a wedding", 舉行婚禮 "hold a wedding". 婚 is built from 女 and 昏, which sounds alike. For the legal side, 結婚 is the word for getting married.

column3: Children as a group, in a formal or official tone: 儿童医院 "children's hospital", 儿童节 "Children's Day", 儿童票. In ordinary speech you say 孩子. 童 is the child, and it is the 童 of 童年.
column4: 这个公园里有很多儿童。
column5: 這個公園裡有很多兒童。
column6: Zhège gōngyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō értóng.
column7: There are many children in this park.
column9: Children as a group, in a formal or official tone: 兒童醫院 "children's hospital", 兒童節 "Children's Day", 兒童票. In ordinary speech you say 孩子. 童 is the child, and it is the 童 of 童年.

column3: An "adult": 成人票 is an adult ticket, 成人教育 adult education. As a verb it means "to grow up": 长大成人. It is more formal than 大人, which children and parents say in speech. Its opposite is 儿童 or 未成年人.
column4: 他已经是成人了，可以自己决定。
column5: 他已經是成人了，可以自己決定。
column6: Tā yǐjīng shì chéngrén le, kěyǐ zìjǐ juédìng.
column7: He's an adult now and can decide for himself.
column9: An "adult": 成人票 is an adult ticket, 成人教育 adult education. As a verb it means "to grow up": 長大成人. It is more formal than 大人, which children and parents say in speech. Its opposite is 兒童 or 未成年人.

column3: A polite word for a "man" or "gentleman", used on signs, in shops and in service talk: 男士 in front of a department, 这位男士 "this gentleman". Its pair is 女士. 士 is also used for polite words for people in other jobs, as in 护士.
column4: 请问这位男士需要什么？
column5: 請問這位男士需要什麼？
column6: Qǐngwèn zhè wèi nánshì xūyào shénme?
column7: Excuse me, what does this gentleman need?
column9: A polite word for a "man" or "gentleman", used on signs, in shops and in service talk: 男士 in front of a department, 這位男士 "this gentleman". Its pair is 女士. 士 is also used for polite words for people in other jobs, as in 護士.

column3: A polite word for a "lady", "Ms.": 女士们，先生们 "ladies and gentlemen", 这位女士. It is also used on signs for women's goods. Its pair is 男士. It fits a woman of any age whom you do not know or want to address politely.
column4: 这位女士是我们的经理。
column5: 這位女士是我們的經理。
column6: Zhè wèi nǚshì shì wǒmen de jīnglǐ.
column7: This lady is our manager.
column9: A polite word for a "lady", "Ms.": 女士們，先生們 "ladies and gentlemen", 這位女士. It is also used on signs for women's goods. Its pair is 男士. It fits a woman of any age whom you do not know or want to address politely.

column3: Men and women, always in that order: 男女老少 "men, women, old and young", 男女平等 "equality of the sexes". It names both groups at once and is often used with 都: 男女都可以. Compare 男女朋友.
column6: Nánnǚ dōu kěyǐ cānjiā bǐsài.
column7: Both men and women can enter the competition.
column9: Men and women, always in that order: 男女老少 "men, women, old and young", 男女平等 "equality of the sexes". It names both groups at once and is often used with 都: 男女都可以. Compare 男女朋友.

column3: A "beautiful woman", often said as a friendly or flattering address to a young woman, especially by shop and market staff: 美女，要不要看看？ Said among friends, it is a compliment; it can sound pushy from a stranger. 美 is a person 大 under a horned headdress 羊.
column6: Měinǚ, nǐ yào mǎi shénme?
column7: Miss, what would you like to buy?
column9: A "beautiful woman", often said as a friendly or flattering address to a young woman, especially by shop and market staff: 美女，要不要看看？ Said among friends, it is a compliment; it can sound pushy from a stranger. 美 is a person 大 under a horned headdress 羊.

column3: Handsome, dashing, used for men: 他很帅. It also means "cool" for anything stylish: 这个动作很帅. In older or formal use 帅 is also a "commander", as in 元帅, and the general in Chinese chess. The left part 刂 stands for a weapon and 巾 for a flag.
column6: Tā yòu gāo yòu shuài.
column7: He is tall and handsome.
column9: Handsome, dashing, used for men: 他很帥. It also means "cool" for anything stylish: 這個動作很帥. In older or formal use 帥 is also a "commander", as in 元帥, and the general in Chinese chess. In 帥 the left part is 丿 over 㠯, and 巾 is on the right.

column3: Handsome guy, also a casual, flattering way for shop staff and strangers to address a young man: 帅哥，要不要看看？ Between friends it teases or compliments. Its pair is 美女. Built from 帅 "handsome" plus 哥 "older brother", the same 哥 as in 大哥.
column6: Shuàigē, yào bù yào jìnlái kànkan?
column7: Hey there, would you like to come in and have a look?
column9: Handsome guy, also a casual, flattering way for shop staff and strangers to address a young man: 帥哥，要不要看看？ Between friends it teases or compliments. Its pair is 美女. Built from 帥 "handsome" plus 哥 "older brother", the same 哥 as in 大哥.

column3: A "young man, lad" in speech, meant warmly and said by someone older: 这个小伙子. It suits a man roughly in his teens up to thirty. In 伙 the 亻 is a person and 火 gives the sound, which still matches (huǒ).
column6: Zhège xiǎohuǒzi hěn yǒu lǐmào.
column7: This young man is very polite.
column9: A "young man, lad" in speech, meant warmly and said by someone older: 這個小夥子. It suits a man roughly in his teens up to thirty. In 夥 the 多 gives the meaning and 果 gives the sound (huǒ).

column3: A "fat person". Calling someone 胖子 to their face is rude; it is mostly used about a third person or a character, or by friends joking. Use the adjective 胖 to say someone is fat: 他很胖. 胖 has 肉 (flesh) on the left and 半 on the right, which gives the sound.
column4: 他以前是个胖子，现在很瘦。
column5: 他以前是個胖子，現在很瘦。
column6: Tā yǐqián shì ge pàngzi, xiànzài hěn shòu.
column7: He used to be fat, but now he is thin.
column9: A "fat person". Calling someone 胖子 to their face is rude; it is mostly used about a third person or a character, or by friends joking. Use the adjective 胖 to say someone is fat: 他很胖. 胖 has 肉 (flesh) on the left and 半 on the right, which gives the sound.

column3: Childhood, the years of being a child: 美好的童年 "a happy childhood", 童年的回忆 "childhood memories". Often used with 在…度过 or 回忆. It is 童 "child" plus 年 "year".
column4: 我的童年是在农村度过的。
column5: 我的童年是在農村度過的。
column6: Wǒ de tóngnián shì zài nóngcūn dùguò de.
column7: I spent my childhood in the countryside.
column9: Childhood, the years of being a child: 美好的童年 "a happy childhood", 童年的回憶 "childhood memories". Often used with 在…度過 or 回憶. It is 童 "child" plus 年 "year".

column3: Kindergarten, the school for children of about three to six: 上幼儿园 "go to kindergarten". 幼 is 幺 ("tiny") plus 力 ("strength"), so a child with little strength. In pinyin an apostrophe separates yòu and ér. After it come 小学 and 中学.
column6: Wǒ nǚ'ér zài shàng yòu'éryuán.
column7: My daughter goes to kindergarten.
column9: Kindergarten, the school for children of about three to six: 上幼兒園 "go to kindergarten". 幼 is 幺 ("tiny") plus 力 ("strength"), so a child with little strength. In pinyin an apostrophe separates yòu and ér. After it come 小學 and 中學.

column3: Youth as a time of life, with a sense of energy and a lost, exciting time: 青春期 "adolescence", 青春的回忆. Both parts belong to nature: 青 is fresh green and 春 is spring, so "green spring". It is used of people, not things.
column4: 这是一部关于青春的电影。
column5: 這是一部關於青春的電影。
column6: Zhè shì yī bù guānyú qīngchūn de diànyǐng.
column7: This is a movie about youth.
column9: Youth as a time of life, with a sense of energy and a lost, exciting time: 青春期 "adolescence", 青春的回憶. Both parts belong to nature: 青 is fresh green and 春 is spring, so "green spring". It is used of people, not things.

column3: A "good friend, close friend": 我的好友, 多年的好友. On social media 加好友 means to add someone as a friend, and 好友 is the friends list. It is a little more written than 好朋友. 友 has two hands, for friendship.
column6: Wǒmen shì duōnián de hǎoyǒu.
column7: We have been close friends for many years.
column9: A "good friend, close friend": 我的好友, 多年的好友. On social media 加好友 means to add someone as a friend, and 好友 is the friends list. It is a little more written than 好朋友. 友 has two hands, for friendship.

column3: A "companion, partner": someone you do something with, such as 学习伙伴 or 好伙伴. In business 合作伙伴 means "partner" in cooperation. Both characters have 亻 "person" and a sound part (火 and 半) that still sounds like them.
column6: Xiǎogǒu shì háizi de hǎo huǒbàn.
column7: The puppy is the child's good companion.
column9: A "companion, partner": someone you do something with, such as 學習伙伴 or 好伙伴. In business 合作夥伴 means "partner" in cooperation. Both characters have 亻 "person" and a sound part (火 and 半) that still sounds like them.

column3: A "famous person, celebrity": 名人 are people the public knows, such as stars and writers. It also appears in 名人名言 "famous sayings". 名 shows a mouth 口 under an evening moon 夕, saying your name in the dark.
column6: Zhè wèi míngrén chángcháng shàng diànshì.
column7: This famous person is often on television.
column9: A "famous person, celebrity": 名人 are people the public knows, such as stars and writers. It also appears in 名人名言 "famous sayings". 名 shows a mouth 口 under an evening moon 夕, saying your name in the dark.

column3: Poor people, the poor as a group, used about people in general: 帮助穷人 "help the poor". For one person you say 他很穷. 穷 as an adjective means "poor".
column6: Tā bāngzhù guo hěn duō qióngrén.
column7: He has helped many poor people.
column9: Poor people, the poor as a group, used about people in general: 幫助窮人 "help the poor". For one person you say 他很窮. 窮 as an adjective means "poor".

column3: A "resident" of a place: 小区居民 "residents of a housing area", 城市居民 "city dwellers". It is a formal, written word used in notices and news. 居 has the door radical 户 and 古 for the sound, 民 is "people".
column6: Xiǎoqū de jūmín dōu hěn yǒuhǎo.
column7: The residents of the neighborhood are all friendly.
column9: A "resident" of a place: 小區居民 "residents of a housing area", 城市居民 "city dwellers". It is a formal, written word used in notices and news. 居 has the door radical 戶 and 古 for the sound, 民 is "people".

column3: Three uses, all spoken. "Other people" in general: 别学人家. "He, she, they" for someone you both know: 人家已经走了. And a coy "I, me": 人家不想去嘛. The 家 is neutral. With the first tone, rénjiā means "household" or "family" and is a different word.
column6: Bié chǎo le, rénjia zài shuìjiào.
column7: Stop making noise, they are sleeping.
column9: Three uses, all spoken. "Other people" in general: 別學人家. "He, she, they" for someone you both know: 人家已經走了. And a coy "I, me": 人家不想去嘛. The 家 is neutral. With the first tone, rénjiā means "household" or "family" and is a different word.

column3: Melon, gourd, squash, any fruit of the vine family. It is the root of many names: 西瓜, 黄瓜, 南瓜. The character is a picture of a melon hanging from its vine. Eating melons, 吃瓜, also became Internet talk for watching the gossip.
column6: Zhège guā yòu dà yòu tián.
column7: This melon is big and sweet.
column9: Melon, gourd, squash, any fruit of the vine family. It is the root of many names: 西瓜, 黃瓜, 南瓜. The character is a picture of a melon hanging from its vine. Eating melons, 吃瓜, also became Internet talk for watching the gossip.

column3: Watermelon, literally "west melon": 西 "west" plus 瓜 "melon". The usual summer fruit: 吃西瓜, 切西瓜 "cut a watermelon". Its measure word is 个 for a whole one and 块 for a slice.
column6: Xiàtiān wǒ zuì ài chī xīguā.
column7: In summer I love eating watermelon most.
column9: Watermelon, literally "west melon": 西 "west" plus 瓜 "melon". The usual summer fruit: 吃西瓜, 切西瓜 "cut a watermelon". Its measure word is 個 for a whole one and 塊 for a slice.

column3: Cucumber: 黄 "yellow" plus 瓜 "melon", though the cucumber you buy is green. It is used raw in salads, as in 拍黄瓜, a cold smashed cucumber dish. Count it with 根 for the long shape: 一根黄瓜.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī gēn huángguā.
column7: I want to buy a cucumber.
column9: Cucumber: 黃 "yellow" plus 瓜 "melon", though the cucumber you buy is green. It is used raw in salads, as in 拍黃瓜, a cold smashed cucumber dish. Count it with 根 for the long shape: 一根黃瓜.

column3: Tofu, bean curd: 豆 "bean" plus 腐, a word for rotting or going soft, which has 肉 inside. Count it with 块: 一块豆腐. The 腐 is neutral. Varieties include 臭豆腐 "stinky tofu" and 麻婆豆腐.
column6: Dòufu shì yòng dòuzi zuò de.
column7: Tofu is made from soybeans.
column9: Tofu, bean curd: 豆 "bean" plus 腐, a word for rotting or going soft, which has 肉 inside. Count it with 塊: 一塊豆腐. The 腐 is neutral. Varieties include 臭豆腐 "stinky tofu" and 麻婆豆腐.

column3: Corn, maize: 玉 "jade" plus 米 "rice", so jade-colored grain. 米 is a picture of grains of rice. You can eat 玉米 boiled on the cob (煮玉米), as a soup or as 玉米粥. 玉 is jade, a precious stone.
column6: Xiàtiān de yùmǐ hěn tián.
column7: Summer corn is very sweet.
column9: Corn, maize: 玉 "jade" plus 米 "rice", so jade-colored grain. 米 is a picture of grains of rice. You can eat 玉米 boiled on the cob (煮玉米), as a soup or as 玉米粥. 玉 is jade, a precious stone.

column3: Seafood: 海 "sea" plus 鲜 "fresh", fish and shellfish in general. 鲜 has 鱼 "fish" and 羊 "sheep", two foods together, so "fresh" and "delicious". Typical use: 吃海鲜, 海鲜过敏 "an allergy to seafood".
column6: Wǒ duì hǎixiān guòmǐn.
column7: I am allergic to seafood.
column9: Seafood: 海 "sea" plus 鮮 "fresh", fish and shellfish in general. 鮮 has 魚 "fish" and 羊 "sheep", two foods together, so "fresh" and "delicious". Typical use: 吃海鮮, 海鮮過敏 "an allergy to seafood".

column3: Snacks, things eaten between meals: 吃零食. 零 means odd bits and small amounts (零钱 "small change"), and 食 is "food". It is a plural word with no measure word: 很多零食 "a lot of snacks".
column6: Háizimen dōu ài chī língshí.
column7: The children all love eating snacks.
column9: Snacks, things eaten between meals: 吃零食. 零 means odd bits and small amounts (零錢 "small change"), and 食 is "food". It is a plural word with no measure word: 很多零食 "a lot of snacks".

column3: Grain, food crops as a staple, in farming and national contexts: 粮食生产 "grain production", 浪费粮食 "waste food". It is not the word for a meal, which is 饭. 粮 has 米 "grain" and 良, a sound that is still close (liáng), and 食 is neutral.
column6: Nóngmín zhòng le hěn duō liángshi.
column7: The farmers grew a lot of grain.
column9: Grain, food crops as a staple, in farming and national contexts: 糧食生產 "grain production", 浪費糧食 "waste food". It is not the word for a meal, which is 飯. 糧 has 米 "grain" and 良, a sound that is still close (liáng), and 食 is neutral.

column3: The "fruit" of a plant in the botanical sense, or in a figure the "fruits" of work: 劳动果实 or 胜利的果实. For eating, the everyday word is 水果. 果 is a picture of fruit 田 growing on a tree 木.
column6: Zhè shì wǒmen nǔlì de guǒshí.
column7: This is the fruit of our hard work.
column9: The "fruit" of a plant in the botanical sense, or in a figure the "fruits" of work: 勞動果實 or 勝利的果實. For eating, the everyday word is 水果. 果 is a picture of fruit 田 growing on a tree 木.

column3: Salt: 放盐 "add salt", 少放点盐 "use a bit less salt". Salt is counted by 勺 or 点, not by a measure word for pieces: 一勺盐. Related words are 食盐 "table salt" and 海盐 "sea salt", and 咸 "salty" describes the taste.
column6: Tāng lǐ zài fàng diǎnr yán.
column7: Add a little more salt to the soup.
column9: Salt: 放鹽 "add salt", 少放點鹽 "use a bit less salt". Salt is counted by 勺 or 點, not by a measure word for pieces: 一勺鹽. Related words are 食鹽 "table salt" and 海鹽 "sea salt", and 鹹 "salty" describes the taste.

column3: A "set meal" with a main dish and sides at a fixed price: 点套餐, 午餐套餐. It is also used for any "package" of services: 手机套餐 "phone plan". 套 "set, cover" plus 餐 "meal", the latter with 食 as its meaning part.
column6: Wǒ yào yī ge tàocān.
column7: I'd like a set meal.
column9: A "set meal" with a main dish and sides at a fixed price: 點套餐, 午餐套餐. It is also used for any "package" of services: 手機套餐 "phone plan". 套 "set, cover" plus 餐 "meal", the latter with 食 as its meaning part.

column3: A "canteen, dining hall" at a school, company or factory: 学校食堂, 在食堂吃饭. It is cheaper and more basic than a restaurant. 食 is "food" and 堂 is a hall.
column4: 中午我们在学校食堂吃饭。
column5: 中午我們在學校食堂吃飯。
column6: Zhōngwǔ wǒmen zài xuéxiào shítáng chīfàn.
column7: At noon we eat at the school canteen.
column9: A "canteen, dining hall" at a school, company or factory: 學校食堂, 在食堂吃飯. It is cheaper and more basic than a restaurant. 食 is "food" and 堂 is a hall.

column3: A "refrigerator": 冰 "ice" plus 箱 "box". Things are put into it with 放进冰箱 or said to be 在冰箱里. 箱 has 竹 (shown as ⺮) for "bamboo" on top, since boxes were once woven from it, and 相 below, which gives the sound.
column6: Niúnǎi zài bīngxiāng lǐ.
column7: The milk is in the fridge.
column9: A "refrigerator": 冰 "ice" plus 箱 "box". Things are put into it with 放進冰箱 or said to be 在冰箱裡. 箱 has 竹 (shown as ⺮) for "bamboo" on top, since boxes were once woven from it, and 相 below, which gives the sound.

column3: A "plate, dish" for serving or eating: 一个盘子, 洗盘子 "wash the dishes". 盘子 is flatter than a bowl (碗). The 盘 has 舟 over 皿 "dish". The 子 is neutral.
column6: Qǐng bǎ pánzi fàng zài zhuōzi shàng.
column7: Please put the plate on the table.
column9: A "plate, dish" for serving or eating: 一個盤子, 洗盤子 "wash the dishes". 盤子 is flatter than a bowl (碗). The 盤 has 般 over 皿 "dish". The 子 is neutral.

column3: Yogurt: 酸 "sour" plus 奶 "milk". It is drunk as a thick drink or eaten with a spoon; count it with 杯 or 盒. 酸 has 酉 "liquor" on the left, the sour taste of wine that has stood too long.
column6: Wǒ zǎofàn hē le yī bēi suānnǎi.
column7: I had a glass of yogurt for breakfast.
column9: Yogurt: 酸 "sour" plus 奶 "milk". It is drunk as a thick drink or eaten with a spoon; count it with 杯 or 盒. 酸 has 酉 "liquor" on the left, the sour taste of wine that has stood too long.

column3: Soda, fizzy drink: 汽 "gas, steam" plus 水 "water". A more formal name is 碳酸饮料. The 氵 water radical on 汽 goes with 气 "air", which gives the sound: water plus air.
column6: Háizi xiǎng hē qìshuǐ.
column7: The child wants to drink soda.
column9: Soda, fizzy drink: 汽 "gas, steam" plus 水 "water". A more formal name is 碳酸飲料. The 氵 water radical on 汽 goes with 气 "air", which gives the sound: water plus air.

column3: Mineral water, bottled spring water: 一瓶矿泉水. 矿 "mineral, ore" has 石 "stone", 泉 is "spring" and looks like water flowing out of a spring mouth. It is what most people just call 水 when buying a bottle.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī píng kuàngquánshuǐ.
column7: Please give me a bottle of mineral water.
column9: Mineral water, bottled spring water: 一瓶礦泉水. 礦 "mineral, ore" has 石 "stone", 泉 is "spring" and looks like water flowing out of a spring mouth. It is what most people just call 水 when buying a bottle.

column3: Purified water, bottled water that has been filtered, with no minerals added. 纯 "pure" and 净 "clean". It is sold beside 矿泉水.
column4: 这瓶是纯净水，不是矿泉水。
column5: 這瓶是純淨水，不是礦泉水。
column6: Zhè píng shì chúnjìngshuǐ, bù shì kuàngquánshuǐ.
column7: This bottle is purified water, not mineral water.
column9: Purified water, bottled water that has been filtered, with no minerals added. 純 "pure" and 淨 "clean". It is sold beside 礦泉水.

column3: Boiled water or hot drinking water, which many Chinese drink instead of cold: 喝开水, 烧开水 "boil water". A common thing to ask for in a restaurant or on a train.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī bēi kāishuǐ.
column7: Please give me a glass of hot water.
column9: Boiled water or hot drinking water, which many Chinese drink instead of cold: 喝開水, 燒開水 "boil water". A common thing to ask for in a restaurant or on a train.

column3: Tea leaves, the dry leaves that you buy and brew, not the drink itself: 一盒茶叶, 买茶叶. The drink is 茶, or 茶水. Tea is graded by origin, e.g. 绿茶 or 红茶.
column4: 这种茶叶是从云南来的。
column5: 這種茶葉是從雲南來的。
column6: Zhè zhǒng cháyè shì cóng Yúnnán lái de.
column7: This tea comes from Yunnan.
column9: Tea leaves, the dry leaves that you buy and brew, not the drink itself: 一盒茶葉, 買茶葉. The drink is 茶, or 茶水. Tea is graded by origin, e.g. 綠茶 or 紅茶.

column3: A "bar" where one drinks alcohol and often listens to music: 去酒吧, 酒吧里. 酒 is "alcohol" and 吧 is a sound borrowed from English "bar". This 吧 is not the particle 吧 that ends a suggestion, though it is written the same.
column4: 周末我们去酒吧听音乐。
column5: 週末我們去酒吧聽音樂。
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù jiǔbā tīng yīnyuè.
column7: At the weekend we go to a bar to listen to music.
column9: A "bar" where one drinks alcohol and often listens to music: 去酒吧, 酒吧裡. 酒 is "alcohol" and 吧 is a sound borrowed from English "bar". This 吧 is not the particle 吧 that ends a suggestion, though it is written the same.

column3: A "drinking straw": 一根吸管. 吸 is "to suck in" and 管 is a "tube", which has a bamboo radical 竹 (⺮) on top, since pipes were once made of bamboo. Typical: 用吸管喝.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī gēn xīguǎn.
column7: Please give me a straw.
column9: A "drinking straw": 一根吸管. 吸 is "to suck in" and 管 is a "tube", which has a bamboo radical 竹 (⺮) on top, since pipes were once made of bamboo. Typical: 用吸管喝.

column3: To breathe in, suck in, also "to absorb": 吸气 "inhale", 吸水 "absorb water". The mouth 口 on the left is the meaning part and 及 gives the sound. Also found in 吸烟 "to smoke" and 吸引 "to attract".
column6: Tā shēnshēn de xī le yī kǒu qì.
column7: He took a deep breath.
column9: To breathe in, suck in, also "to absorb": 吸氣 "inhale", 吸水 "absorb water". The mouth 口 on the left is the meaning part and 及 gives the sound. Also found in 吸煙 "to smoke" and 吸引 "to attract".

column3: Spicy, hot from chili peppers or mustard: 辣椒 "chili pepper", 不辣 "not spicy", 辣的菜. Sichuan and Hunan dishes are known for it. The left part 辛 means a sharp, bitter taste, and the right part 束 gives the sound.
column4: 这个菜太辣了，我不能吃。
column5: 這個菜太辣了，我不能吃。
column6: Zhège cài tài là le, wǒ bù néng chī.
column7: This dish is too spicy, I can't eat it.
column9: Spicy, hot from chili peppers or mustard: 辣椒 "chili pepper", 不辣 "not spicy", 辣的菜. Sichuan and Hunan dishes are known for it. The left part 辛 means a sharp, bitter taste, and the right part 束 gives the sound.

column3: Sour, the taste of vinegar or lemon: 酸奶, 酸辣汤. It also means "sore, aching" of muscles: 腿很酸 "my legs ache". The left part 酉 is a wine jar, so the character pictures a drink that has turned.
column6: Zhège píngguǒ tài suān le.
column7: This apple is too sour.
column9: Sour, the taste of vinegar or lemon: 酸奶, 酸辣湯. It also means "sore, aching" of muscles: 腿很酸 "my legs ache". The left part 酉 is a wine jar, so the character pictures a drink that has turned.

column3: Salty: 太咸了 "too salty". Its opposite is 淡.
column6: Tāng tài xián le.
column7: The soup is too salty.
column9: Salty: 太鹹了 "too salty". Its opposite is 淡.

column3: Bitter: 药很苦. It also means "hard, painful" in 吃苦 "endure hardship" and 辛苦 "hard work, tiring". 艹 "grass" on top is the meaning part, a bitter herb, and 古 gives the sound.
column6: Zhège yào hěn kǔ.
column7: This medicine is very bitter.
column9: Bitter: 藥很苦. It also means "hard, painful" in 吃苦 "endure hardship" and 辛苦 "hard work, tiring". 艹 "grass" on top is the meaning part, a bitter herb, and 古 gives the sound.

column3: Bland, weak, light: of taste (汤很淡, the opposite of 咸), of tea or color (淡蓝色 "light blue"), and of feelings (冷淡 "cold, indifferent"). 氵 "water" and 炎, which gives the sound.
column6: Zhè wǎn tāng yǒudiǎnr dàn.
column7: This bowl of soup is a bit bland.
column9: Bland, weak, light: of taste (湯很淡, the opposite of 鹹), of tea or color (淡藍色 "light blue"), and of feelings (冷淡 "cold, indifferent"). 氵 "water" and 炎, which gives the sound.

column3: Thick, strong, concentrated: of taste, smell, color or tea (浓茶), and of feelings (感情很浓). The opposite is 淡.
column6: Zhè bēi kāfēi tài nóng le.
column7: This cup of coffee is too strong.
column9: Thick, strong, concentrated: of taste, smell, color or tea (濃茶), and of feelings (感情很濃). The opposite is 淡.

column3: Fresh of food, and "tasty, delicious" in the way fresh fish and shellfish are: 这条鱼很鲜. The character joins 鱼 "fish" and 羊 "sheep", two foods. Also "bright" in color, as in 鲜花 and 鲜红. It is mostly met inside words such as 新鲜 and 海鲜.
column6: Zhè tiáo yú hěn xiān.
column7: This fish is very tasty.
column9: Fresh of food, and "tasty, delicious" in the way fresh fish and shellfish are: 這條魚很鮮. The character joins 魚 "fish" and 羊 "sheep", two foods. Also "bright" in color, as in 鮮花 and 鮮紅. It is mostly met inside words such as 新鮮 and 海鮮.

column3: Fresh: food (新鲜的水果), air (新鲜空气), and also "new and interesting": 新鲜事 "a novelty". It is formed from 新 "new" and 鲜 "fresh". For a new thing that has just been made, use 新 alone.
column6: Zhèlǐ de kōngqì hěn xīnxiān.
column7: The air here is fresh.
column9: Fresh: food (新鮮的水果), air (新鮮空氣), and also "new and interesting": 新鮮事 "a novelty". It is formed from 新 "new" and 鮮 "fresh". For a new thing that has just been made, use 新 alone.

column3: Taste, smell, the colloquial erhua form of 味道, common in the north: 这个菜的味儿不错, 烟味儿 "smell of smoke". The 儿 is not a separate syllable; it only changes the ending: wèir. In writing the standard word is 味道.
column6: Zhège cài de wèir bùcuò.
column7: This dish tastes quite good.
column9: Taste, smell, the colloquial erhua form of 味道, common in the north: 這個菜的味兒不錯, 煙味兒 "smell of smoke". The 兒 is not a separate syllable; it only changes the ending: wèir. In writing the standard word is 味道.

column3: Window: 开窗户 "open a window". The 户 is neutral here. 窗 has 穴 "hole" on top, as a window is an opening in a wall. 窗子 means the same, and 窗 alone is mostly in compounds.
column6: Qǐng bǎ chuānghu dǎkāi.
column7: Please open the window.
column9: Window: 開窗戶 "open a window". The 戶 is neutral here. 窗 has 穴 "hole" on top, as a window is an opening in a wall. 窗子 means the same, and 窗 alone is mostly in compounds.

column3: Windowsill, window ledge: 窗台上 "on the windowsill". 窗 is "window" and 台 a "platform", a flat place for putting things such as flowerpots.
column6: Huā fàng zài chuāngtái shàng.
column7: The flowers are on the windowsill.
column9: Windowsill, window ledge: 窗臺上 "on the windowsill". 窗 is "window" and 臺 a "platform", a flat place for putting things such as flowerpots.

column3: Window, the spoken word, same as 窗户 and heard more in the north: 窗子外面. The 子 is a neutral suffix. 窗户 is about as common, and 窗 is the part you see in compounds like 窗帘 "curtain".
column6: Tā zhàn zài chuāngzi pángbiān.
column7: He is standing beside the window.
column9: Window, the spoken word, same as 窗戶 and heard more in the north: 窗子外面. The 子 is a neutral suffix. 窗戶 is about as common, and 窗 is the part you see in compounds like 窗簾 "curtain".

column3: A "balcony", the open ledge off an apartment: 在阳台上, 阳台上晒衣服. In many Chinese homes the balcony is where laundry is dried. 阳 is "sun" 日 beside 阝 (hill), the sunny side, the opposite of 阴 "shady".
column6: Wǒmen zài yángtái shàng hē chá.
column7: We are drinking tea on the balcony.
column9: A "balcony", the open ledge off an apartment: 在陽臺上, 陽臺上曬衣服. In many Chinese homes the balcony is where laundry is dried. 陽 is "sun" 日 beside 阝 (hill), the sunny side, the opposite of 陰 "shady".

column3: Stairs, staircase: 上楼梯 "go up the stairs", 楼梯口 "the stair entrance". 楼 is a building with floors and 梯 a ladder or stair; 梯 has 木 "wood", as it was made of wood, and 弟 for the sound (tī, dì).
column6: Xiǎoxīn lóutī, bié shuāidǎo.
column7: Watch the stairs, don't fall.
column9: Stairs, staircase: 上樓梯 "go up the stairs", 樓梯口 "the stair entrance". 樓 is a building with floors and 梯 a ladder or stair; 梯 has 木 "wood", as it was made of wood, and 弟 for the sound (tī, dì).

column3: Steps leading up to a door or building: 门前的台阶, 上台阶. Figuratively, 给他一个台阶下 means giving someone a way out of an embarrassing situation. 阶 has 阝 "hill" because stairs go up a slope.
column6: Ménkǒu yǒu jǐ ge táijiē.
column7: There are a few steps at the door.
column9: Steps leading up to a door or building: 門前的臺階, 上台階. Figuratively, 給他一個臺階下 means giving someone a way out of an embarrassing situation. 階 has 阝 "hill" because stairs go up a slope.

column3: An "elevator": 坐电梯, 乘电梯 "ride the elevator", 等电梯, 电梯里. It adds 电 "electric" to 梯 "stairs".
column6: Wǒmen zuò diàntī shàngqù ba.
column7: Let's take the elevator up.
column9: An "elevator": 坐電梯, 乘電梯 "ride the elevator", 等電梯, 電梯裡. It adds 電 "electric" to 梯 "stairs".

column3: A "large building" with several floors, usually an office, hotel or apartment block: 办公大楼 "office building". 楼 alone is a building or a floor, and 大 stresses the size. The count is 座: 一座大楼.
column6: Nà zuò dàlóu yǒu sānshí céng.
column7: That building has thirty floors.
column9: A "large building" with several floors, usually an office, hotel or apartment block: 辦公大樓 "office building". 樓 alone is a building or a floor, and 大 stresses the size. The count is 座: 一座大樓.

column3: To go upstairs, a verb and its object: 上楼 "go up", 下楼 "go down". You use it for going up in a building, and then 去 or 来 shows the direction: 上楼来 "come up".
column6: Tā mànmàn de shànglóu.
column7: He is going upstairs slowly.
column9: To go upstairs, a verb and its object: 上樓 "go up", 下樓 "go down". You use it for going up in a building, and then 去 or 來 shows the direction: 上樓來 "come up".

column3: To go downstairs, the opposite of 上楼: 下楼买东西 "go down to buy something", 下楼吃饭. In an apartment block, it is the usual way to say you are going out. 下 is the opposite of 上 in shape too: a short stroke below instead of above.
column6: Wǒ xiàlóu mǎi diǎn dōngxi.
column7: I'm going downstairs to buy something.
column9: To go downstairs, the opposite of 上樓: 下樓買東西 "go down to buy something", 下樓吃飯. In an apartment block, it is the usual way to say you are going out. 下 is the opposite of 上 in shape too: a short stroke below instead of above.

column3: Light from lamps or stage lights: 灯光很暗, 舞台灯光. It means light that someone sees, not the lamp itself (灯) and not daylight (阳光). 光 is a person 儿 with fire on the head.
column6: Fángjiān lǐ de dēngguāng hěn wēnnuǎn.
column7: The lamp light in the room is warm.
column9: Light from lamps or stage lights: 燈光很暗, 舞臺燈光. It means light that someone sees, not the lamp itself (燈) and not daylight (陽光). 光 is a person 儿 with fire on the head.

column3: An "electric light": 开电灯 "turn on the light". In everyday speech people simply say 灯: 开灯, 关灯. 电灯 sounds a little old-fashioned or technical, as distinct from candles or oil lamps.
column6: Qǐng bǎ diàndēng guān le.
column7: Please turn off the light.
column9: An "electric light": 開電燈 "turn on the light". In everyday speech people simply say 燈: 開燈, 關燈. 電燈 sounds a little old-fashioned or technical, as distinct from candles or oil lamps.

column3: Central heating in northern China: a radiator system from a heating plant, which runs by season: 开暖气, 有暖气. It is also "warm air" from a heater. 暖 has 日 "sun" on the left and 爰 for the sound, "warm as in the sun".
column4: 冬天屋里有暖气，很暖和。
column5: 冬天屋裡有暖氣，很暖和。
column6: Dōngtiān wū lǐ yǒu nuǎnqì, hěn nuǎnhuo.
column7: In winter there is heating indoors and it's warm.
column9: Central heating in northern China: a radiator system from a heating plant, which runs by season: 開暖氣, 有暖氣. It is also "warm air" from a heater. 暖 has 日 "sun" on the left and 爰 for the sound, "warm as in the sun".

column3: To renovate, to decorate a home or shop: 装修房子, 正在装修. It covers the whole job, with walls, floors and fittings. 装 is "to dress, install" and 修 "to repair". Used as a noun too: 装修很漂亮.
column4: 我们的新房子正在装修。
column5: 我們的新房子正在裝修。
column6: Wǒmen de xīn fángzi zhèngzài zhuāngxiū.
column7: Our new house is being renovated.
column9: To renovate, to decorate a home or shop: 裝修房子, 正在裝修. It covers the whole job, with walls, floors and fittings. 裝 is "to dress, install" and 修 "to repair". Used as a noun too: 裝修很漂亮.

column3: To arrange, set out, decorate a room or an event: 布置房间, 布置会场. Also "to assign" tasks, especially homework: 老师布置作业. 置 means "to place"; its top 罒 is a net, and 直 gives the sound.
column4: 老师给我们布置了作业。
column5: 老師給我們佈置了作業。
column6: Lǎoshī gěi wǒmen bùzhì le zuòyè.
column7: The teacher gave us homework.
column9: To arrange, set out, decorate a room or an event: 佈置房間, 佈置會場. Also "to assign" tasks, especially homework: 老師佈置作業. 置 means "to place"; its top 罒 is a net, and 直 gives the sound.

column3: A "box, case, trunk", but alone mostly a measure word: 一箱水 "a case of water", 一箱书. As a thing it is found in compounds such as 冰箱 and 行李箱. 箱 has 竹 (⺮) because it was once a woven bamboo box, and 相 for the sound.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī xiāng shuǐ.
column7: I bought a case of water.
column9: A "box, case, trunk", but alone mostly a measure word: 一箱水 "a case of water", 一箱書. As a thing it is found in compounds such as 冰箱 and 行李箱. 箱 has 竹 (⺮) because it was once a woven bamboo box, and 相 for the sound.

column3: A "box, trunk, suitcase": 一个箱子, 搬箱子. Suitcases are often 行李箱, but in speech 箱子 is the general word for any big box or case. The 子 is neutral.
column6: Xiāngzi lǐ zhuāngmǎn le shū.
column7: The box is full of books.
column9: A "box, trunk, suitcase": 一個箱子, 搬箱子. Suitcases are often 行李箱, but in speech 箱子 is the general word for any big box or case. The 子 is neutral.

column3: Trash, garbage: 扔垃圾 "throw out the trash", 垃圾桶 "trash can", 垃圾分类 "trash sorting". It is also used for things of poor quality: 垃圾食品 "junk food". Both characters have 土 "earth" on the left and a sound part, and neither occurs alone.
column6: Qǐng bùyào luàn rēng lājī.
column7: Please don't throw trash around.
column9: Trash, garbage: 扔垃圾 "throw out the trash", 垃圾桶 "trash can", 垃圾分類 "trash sorting". It is also used for things of poor quality: 垃圾食品 "junk food". Both characters have 土 "earth" on the left and a sound part, and neither occurs alone.

column3: To clean a room or house by sweeping and tidying: 打扫房间, 打扫卫生. It is the usual word for a general cleaning. 扫 is "to sweep"; the object is the place you clean, not the dirt.
column6: Zhōumò wǒ yào dǎsǎo fángjiān.
column7: I'm going to clean the room at the weekend.
column9: To clean a room or house by sweeping and tidying: 打掃房間, 打掃衛生. It is the usual word for a general cleaning. 掃 is "to sweep"; the object is the place you clean, not the dirt.

column3: To sweep with a broom: 扫地 "sweep the floor", 扫雪. Also "to scan": 扫码 "scan a QR code".
column6: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang sǎo dì.
column7: I sweep the floor every morning.
column9: To sweep with a broom: 掃地 "sweep the floor", 掃雪. Also "to scan": 掃碼 "scan a QR code".

column3: To wipe, rub: 擦桌子 "wipe the table", 擦黑板, 擦汗 "wipe sweat". Also "to put on" cream or polish: 擦药, 擦皮鞋 "polish shoes". 扌 "hand" is the meaning part and 察 gives the sound.
column6: Qǐng nǐ cā yīxià zhuōzi.
column7: Please wipe the table.
column9: To wipe, rub: 擦桌子 "wipe the table", 擦黑板, 擦汗 "wipe sweat". Also "to put on" cream or polish: 擦藥, 擦皮鞋 "polish shoes". 扌 "hand" is the meaning part and 察 gives the sound.

column3: Housework, the tasks of running a home: 做家务 "do housework" is the standard collocation, along with 分担家务 "share the chores". 家 is "home", 务 "affairs, tasks"; It is a written word, but also said in speech.
column6: Tā měitiān bāng māma zuò jiāwù.
column7: He helps his mother with the housework every day.
column9: Housework, the tasks of running a home: 做家務 "do housework" is the standard collocation, along with 分擔家務 "share the chores". 家 is "home", 務 "affairs, tasks"; It is a written word, but also said in speech.

column3: The "ground, floor" as a surface: 地面很滑 "the floor is slippery", 地面上, 擦地面. It speaks of the surface itself, not of the place; 地 is "earth" and 面 "surface, face". For a floor inside a house, 地板 is the material and 地面 the surface.
column6: Xià yǔ hòu, dìmiàn hěn huá.
column7: The ground is slippery after the rain.
column9: The "ground, floor" as a surface: 地面很滑 "the floor is slippery", 地面上, 擦地面. It speaks of the surface itself, not of the place; 地 is "earth" and 面 "surface, face". For a floor inside a house, 地板 is the material and 地面 the surface.

column3: Underground, under the ground: 地下停车场 "underground parking", 地下室 "basement", 地下铁 "subway". Opposite 地上. It can also mean "secret, underground" in a political or hidden sense: 地下工作.
column6: Wǒmen de chē tíng zài dìxià.
column7: Our car is parked underground.
column9: Underground, under the ground: 地下停車場 "underground parking", 地下室 "basement", 地下鐵 "subway". Opposite 地上. It can also mean "secret, underground" in a political or hidden sense: 地下工作.

column3: A "sweater", knitted wool top: 穿毛衣, 一件毛衣. 毛 is "hair, wool" and 衣 "clothes". It is not a coat: for outer clothing there is 外套. 毛 is a picture of a feather or hair.
column6: Tiān lěng le, nǐ gāi chuān máoyī le.
column7: It has turned cold, so you should wear a sweater.
column9: A "sweater", knitted wool top: 穿毛衣, 一件毛衣. 毛 is "hair, wool" and 衣 "clothes". It is not a coat: for outer clothing there is 外套. 毛 is a picture of a feather or hair.

column3: A "hat, cap": 戴帽子 "wear a hat", 一顶帽子. The measure word is 顶. Figuratively 扣帽子 means to pin a label on somebody. 帽 has 巾 "cloth" on the left and 冒 on the right for the sound.
column6: Tā dàizhe yī dǐng hóng màozi.
column7: He is wearing a red hat.
column9: A "hat, cap": 戴帽子 "wear a hat", 一頂帽子. The measure word is 頂. Figuratively 扣帽子 means to pin a label on somebody. 帽 has 巾 "cloth" on the left and 冒 on the right for the sound.

column3: Socks: 一双袜子 "a pair of socks", 穿袜子. The 衤 on the left is the clothes radical, and 末 gives the sound. Count them with 双 for a pair and 只 for one sock.
column6: Wǒ de wàzi pò le.
column7: My socks have a hole.
column9: Socks: 一雙襪子 "a pair of socks", 穿襪子. The 衤 on the left is the clothes radical, and 蔑 gives the sound. Count them with 雙 for a pair and 隻 for one sock.

column3: A "coat, jacket", something worn over other clothes: 穿外套, 一件外套. 外 is "outer" and 套 is a "cover". It covers anything from a light jacket to a winter coat; a long heavy coat can also be called 大衣.
column4: 外面冷，你带一件外套吧。
column5: 外面冷，你帶一件外套吧。
column6: Wàimiàn lěng, nǐ dài yī jiàn wàitào ba.
column7: It's cold outside, take a jacket.
column9: A "coat, jacket", something worn over other clothes: 穿外套, 一件外套. 外 is "outer" and 套 is a "cover". It covers anything from a light jacket to a winter coat; a long heavy coat can also be called 大衣.

column3: A "scarf": 戴围巾 "wear a scarf", 一条围巾. The verb is 戴 or 围: 围围巾 "wrap a scarf around". 围 means "to surround" and 巾 is a hanging piece of cloth, so it is a "cloth that surrounds".
column6: Māma sòng wǒ yī tiáo wéijīn.
column7: Mom gave me a scarf.
column9: A "scarf": 戴圍巾 "wear a scarf", 一條圍巾. The verb is 戴 or 圍: 圍圍巾 "wrap a scarf around". 圍 means "to surround" and 巾 is a hanging piece of cloth, so it is a "cloth that surrounds".

column3: Gloves: 戴手套 "wear gloves", 一副手套 or 一双手套. 手 is "hand" and 套 a "cover", so "a cover for the hand". Gloves with separate fingers and mittens (连指手套) both belong.
column6: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, nǐ yào dài shǒutào.
column7: It's cold outside, you should wear gloves.
column9: Gloves: 戴手套 "wear gloves", 一副手套 or 一雙手套. 手 is "hand" and 套 a "cover", so "a cover for the hand". Gloves with separate fingers and mittens (連指手套) both belong.

column3: To put on clothes, shoes, socks: 穿上外套, 穿上鞋. 上 is a result complement that shows the action is done and the clothes are on you; it is neutral here. The opposite is 脱下. 穿 has 穴 "hole" over 牙 "tooth", the picture of going through.
column6: Kuài chuānshang wàitào, wàimiàn hěn lěng.
column7: Put on a coat quickly, it's cold outside.
column9: To put on clothes, shoes, socks: 穿上外套, 穿上鞋. 上 is a result complement that shows the action is done and the clothes are on you; it is neutral here. The opposite is 脫下. 穿 has 穴 "hole" over 牙 "tooth", the picture of going through.

column3: To wear things that sit on the head, face, neck, hands or wrist: 戴帽子, 戴眼镜, 戴手套, 戴手表. For clothes and shoes the verb is 穿. The old form of the character showed a person holding something on their head with both hands.
column6: Tā měitiān dōu dài màozi.
column7: He wears a hat every day.
column9: To wear things that sit on the head, face, neck, hands or wrist: 戴帽子, 戴眼鏡, 戴手套, 戴手錶. For clothes and shoes the verb is 穿. The old form of the character showed a person holding something on their head with both hands.

column3: To take off clothes and shoes: 脱衣服, 脱鞋, 脱帽. Opposite of 穿. It also means "to get free of": 脱险 "escape danger". 脱 has the flesh radical ⺼ on the left and 兑 on the right.
column6: Jìn mén qǐng tuō xié.
column7: Please take off your shoes when you come in.
column9: To take off clothes and shoes: 脫衣服, 脫鞋, 脫帽. Opposite of 穿. It also means "to get free of": 脫險 "escape danger". 脫 has the flesh radical ⺼ on the left and 兌 on the right.

column3: Glasses: 戴眼镜 "wear glasses", 一副眼镜 (measure word 副). 眼 is "eye", and 镜 is "mirror", with 钅 "metal" on the left as mirrors were once polished metal. Sunglasses are 太阳镜 or 墨镜.
column4: 他戴着一副黑色的眼镜。
column5: 他戴著一副黑色的眼鏡。
column6: Tā dàizhe yī fù hēisè de yǎnjìng.
column7: He is wearing a pair of black glasses.
column9: Glasses: 戴眼鏡 "wear glasses", 一副眼鏡 (measure word 副). 眼 is "eye", and 鏡 is "mirror", with 釒 "metal" on the left as mirrors were once polished metal. Sunglasses are 太陽鏡 or 墨鏡.

column3: Umbrella: 带伞 "bring an umbrella", 打伞 "put up an umbrella", 一把伞. Its measure word is 把, as for things with a handle. The character itself looks like a little umbrella.
column4: 今天会下雨，你带伞了吗？
column5: 今天會下雨，你帶傘了嗎？
column6: Jīntiān huì xiàyǔ, nǐ dài sǎn le ma?
column7: It will rain today, did you bring an umbrella?
column9: Umbrella: 帶傘 "bring an umbrella", 打傘 "put up an umbrella", 一把傘. Its measure word is 把, as for things with a handle. The character itself looks like a little umbrella.

column3: A "mirror": 照镜子 "look in a mirror". 镜 means mirror or lens and is the same 镜 as in 眼镜; the 子 is neutral. 钅 "metal" shows mirrors were once of polished metal. Count it with 面: 一面镜子.
column6: Tā zhèngzài zhào jìngzi.
column7: She is looking in the mirror.
column9: A "mirror": 照鏡子 "look in a mirror". 鏡 means mirror or lens and is the same 鏡 as in 眼鏡; the 子 is neutral. 釒 "metal" shows mirrors were once of polished metal. Count it with 面: 一面鏡子.

column3: A "pocket" on clothes (裤子口袋, 衣服口袋) or a bag: 放进口袋里. It is a spoken word. 口 is "mouth, opening" and 袋 "bag": a bag with an opening. In the north a pocket may also be called 兜.
column6: Yàoshi zài wǒ de kǒudài lǐ.
column7: The key is in my pocket.
column9: A "pocket" on clothes (褲子口袋, 衣服口袋) or a bag: 放進口袋裡. It is a spoken word. 口 is "mouth, opening" and 袋 "bag": a bag with an opening. In the north a pocket may also be called 兜.

column3: Bag, pouch, sack, and a measure word for what comes in one: 一袋米 "a bag of rice", 一袋面粉. On its own it is mostly a measure word or part of 口袋, 塑料袋. 袋 has 衣 "cloth" under 代, which gives the sound (dài).
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī dài dàmǐ.
column7: I bought a bag of rice.
column9: Bag, pouch, sack, and a measure word for what comes in one: 一袋米 "a bag of rice", 一袋麵粉. On its own it is mostly a measure word or part of 口袋, 塑料袋. 袋 has 衣 "cloth" under 代, which gives the sound (dài).

column3: A "plastic bag": 一个塑料袋. 塑料 is "plastic" and 袋 "bag". In Taiwan the usual word is 塑胶袋. In shops you may be asked 要不要袋子？
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī ge sùliàodài.
column7: Please give me a plastic bag.
column9: A "plastic bag": 一個塑料袋. 塑料 is "plastic" and 袋 "bag". In Taiwan the usual word is 塑膠袋. In shops you may be asked 要不要袋子？

column3: Someone's "figure, build": 身材好 "a good figure", 身材高大 "tall and big", 身材苗条 "slim". It covers height and shape together. 身 is "body", 材 is "material", with 木 as the meaning part.
column6: Tā de shēncái hěn hǎo.
column7: She has a good figure.
column9: Someone's "figure, build": 身材好 "a good figure", 身材高大 "tall and big", 身材苗條 "slim". It covers height and shape together. 身 is "body", 材 is "material", with 木 as the meaning part.

column3: The "belly, stomach" area: 肚子疼 "have a stomachache", 肚子饿 "be hungry", 大肚子 "a big belly". It is the spoken word for the whole abdomen. For the digestive organ, the medical word is 胃. 肚 has the flesh radical ⺼ on the left.
column6: Wǒ dùzi è le.
column7: I'm hungry.
column9: The "belly, stomach" area: 肚子疼 "have a stomachache", 肚子餓 "be hungry", 大肚子 "a big belly". It is the spoken word for the whole abdomen. For the digestive organ, the medical word is 胃. 肚 has the flesh radical ⺼ on the left.

column3: The "waist" and also the lower back: 腰疼 "backache", 弯腰 "bend over", 腰带 "belt". Back pain is usually located here. 腰 has ⺼ for flesh and 要 for the sound, which is still close (yāo, yào).
column6: Wǒ de yāo yǒudiǎnr téng.
column7: My lower back hurts a little.
column9: The "waist" and also the lower back: 腰疼 "backache", 彎腰 "bend over", 腰帶 "belt". Back pain is usually located here. 腰 has ⺼ for flesh and 要 for the sound, which is still close (yāo, yào).

column3: Head, the informal spoken word: 摇脑袋 "shake one's head", 脑袋疼. It can also mean one's brains or sense. 头 is the neutral word for the head, and 脑袋 is more casual, sometimes joking. The 袋 is neutral.
column6: Tā yáo le yáo nǎodai.
column7: He shook his head.
column9: Head, the informal spoken word: 搖腦袋 "shake one's head", 腦袋疼. It can also mean one's brains or sense. 頭 is the neutral word for the head, and 腦袋 is more casual, sometimes joking. The 袋 is neutral.

column3: Tooth: 牙疼 "toothache", 刷牙 "brush the teeth", 牙医 "dentist". The measure word is 颗: 一颗牙. The character comes from a picture of two interlocking tusks or teeth. 牙 is also in 牙膏 "toothpaste".
column6: Wǒ de yá hěn téng.
column7: My tooth hurts a lot.
column9: Tooth: 牙疼 "toothache", 刷牙 "brush the teeth", 牙醫 "dentist". The measure word is 顆: 一顆牙. The character comes from a picture of two interlocking tusks or teeth. 牙 is also in 牙膏 "toothpaste".

column3: Bone: 一根骨头, 啃骨头 "gnaw a bone". Also used for the body's frame: 骨头疼. 头 is neutral; it is a suffix and does not mean "head" here. The character 骨 has flesh ⺼ under a picture of bones.
column6: Gǒu xǐhuan chī gǔtou.
column7: Dogs like eating bones.
column9: Bone: 一根骨頭, 啃骨頭 "gnaw a bone". Also used for the body's frame: 骨頭疼. 頭 is neutral; it is a suffix and does not mean "head" here. The character 骨 has flesh ⺼ under a picture of bones.

column3: The "chest, bust" as a part of the body: 胸部疼 "chest pain", 胸部手术. It is a neutral, medical word. In speech 胸 or 胸口 are used. 部 here means "part": 头部 "head", 腹部 "abdomen".
column6: Tā de xiōngbù shòushāng le.
column7: His chest was injured.
column9: The "chest, bust" as a part of the body: 胸部疼 "chest pain", 胸部手術. It is a neutral, medical word. In speech 胸 or 胸口 are used. 部 here means "part": 頭部 "head", 腹部 "abdomen".

column3: A body "organ": 器官移植 "organ transplant", 内脏器官. 器 is an "instrument, vessel" and 官 is "official"; together they name the parts of the body that each do a job. Examples are 心脏 "heart" and 肺 "lungs".
column6: Xīnzàng shì zhòngyào de qìguān.
column7: The heart is an important organ.
column9: A body "organ": 器官移植 "organ transplant", 內臟器官. 器 is an "instrument, vessel" and 官 is "official"; together they name the parts of the body that each do a job. Examples are 心臟 "heart" and 肺 "lungs".

column3: To breathe: 呼吸空气, 呼吸困难 "difficulty breathing", 深呼吸 "deep breath". It joins 呼 "breathe out" and 吸 "breathe in", two opposite actions put together.
column4: 在公园里可以呼吸新鲜空气。
column5: 在公園裡可以呼吸新鮮空氣。
column6: Zài gōngyuán lǐ kěyǐ hūxī xīnxiān kōngqì.
column7: In the park you can breathe fresh air.
column9: To breathe: 呼吸空氣, 呼吸困難 "difficulty breathing", 深呼吸 "deep breath". It joins 呼 "breathe out" and 吸 "breathe in", two opposite actions put together.

column3: Tears, in the phrase 流泪 "shed tears" and in 眼泪, 泪水. It rarely stands alone otherwise, and is literary. The character is a picture: water 氵 from the eye 目.
column6: Tā gǎndòng de liú lèi le.
column7: She was moved to tears.
column9: Tears, in the phrase 流淚 "shed tears" and in 眼淚, 淚水. It rarely stands alone otherwise, and is literary. The character has water 氵 and 戾 as its sound.

column3: Tears, with a more literary and emotional ring: 泪水流下来, 充满泪水. For a plain statement people say 眼泪. 泪 is "tear" and 水 "water", the same 泪 as in 流泪. 水 is a picture of flowing water.
column4: 泪水从她的脸上流下来。
column5: 淚水從她的臉上流下來。
column6: Lèishuǐ cóng tā de liǎn shàng liú xiàlái.
column7: Tears ran down her face.
column9: Tears, with a more literary and emotional ring: 淚水流下來, 充滿淚水. For a plain statement people say 眼淚. 淚 is "tear" and 水 "water", the same 淚 as in 流淚. 水 is a picture of flowing water.

column3: Tears (the drop): 流眼泪 "shed tears", 擦眼泪 "wipe tears". It is the plain, everyday word, more common than 泪水 in speech. 眼 "eye" plus 泪 "tear".
column6: Tā cā le cā yǎnlèi.
column7: He wiped his tears.
column9: Tears (the drop): 流眼淚 "shed tears", 擦眼淚 "wipe tears". It is the plain, everyday word, more common than 淚水 in speech. 眼 "eye" plus 淚 "tear".

column3: A person's "height": 身高一米八 "1.8 m tall", 你的身高是多少？ It is used for people, while 高度 is for buildings and mountains. 身 is the "body" and 高 "tall".
column6: Tā de shēngāo yǒu yī mǐ bā.
column7: He is 1.8 meters tall.
column9: A person's "height": 身高一米八 "1.8 m tall", 你的身高是多少？ It is used for people, while 高度 is for buildings and mountains. 身 is the "body" and 高 "tall".

column3: Body weight: 量体重 "weigh oneself", 体重增加 "gain weight", 减轻体重. The unit is 公斤 (kilogram) or 斤 (half a kilogram), and you can ask 你多重？ The reading of 重 here is zhòng, not chóng.
column6: Wǒ de tǐzhòng shì wǔshí gōngjīn.
column7: My weight is fifty kilograms.
column9: Body weight: 量體重 "weigh oneself", 體重增加 "gain weight", 減輕體重. The unit is 公斤 (kilogram) or 斤 (half a kilogram), and you can ask 你多重？ The reading of 重 here is zhòng, not chóng.

column3: Physical "strength": 有力气 "be strong", 用力气, 没力气 "have no strength". Speaking of muscle power, not of will or ability. The 气 is neutral. 力 is a picture of a plow or an arm, the strength of the body.
column4: 他力气很大，一个人搬得动。
column5: 他力氣很大，一個人搬得動。
column6: Tā lìqi hěn dà, yī ge rén bān de dòng.
column7: He is strong and can move it by himself.
column9: Physical "strength": 有力氣 "be strong", 用力氣, 沒力氣 "have no strength". Speaking of muscle power, not of will or ability. The 氣 is neutral. 力 is a picture of a plow or an arm, the strength of the body.

column3: Mental and physical "energy": 精力充沛 "full of energy", 没有精力 "have no energy for". It is the energy to do things over time, not a burst of strength like 力气. 精 has 米 "rice", for refined grain, and 青 for the sound.
column6: Wǒ méiyǒu jīnglì zài xuéxí le.
column7: I have no energy left to study.
column9: Mental and physical "energy": 精力充沛 "full of energy", 沒有精力 "have no energy for". It is the energy to do things over time, not a burst of strength like 力氣. 精 has 米 "rice", for refined grain, and 青 for the sound.

column3: Heredity, to be inherited: 遗传基因 "genes", 这种病会遗传 "this illness is hereditary". It is the passing of traits from parent to child. 遗 is "to leave behind" (辶 and 贵 "valuable") and 传 "to pass on".
column6: Zhè zhǒng bìng huì yíchuán.
column7: This illness can be inherited.
column9: Heredity, to be inherited: 遺傳基因 "genes", 這種病會遺傳 "this illness is hereditary". It is the passing of traits from parent to child. 遺 is "to leave behind" (辶 and 貴 "valuable") and 傳 "to pass on".

column3: To digest: 消化食物, 消化不良 "indigestion", 不容易消化 "hard to digest". Also figuratively "to absorb, take in" what you learn: 消化新知识. 消 is "to dissolve" with 氵 "water" and 化 "to change", so food dissolves and changes.
column6: Chī tài duō bù róngyì xiāohuà.
column7: If you eat too much it is hard to digest.
column9: To digest: 消化食物, 消化不良 "indigestion", 不容易消化 "hard to digest". Also figuratively "to absorb, take in" what you learn: 消化新知識. 消 is "to dissolve" with 氵 "water" and 化 "to change", so food dissolves and changes.

column3: Short and small, for a person or a building, a little unflattering: 身材矮小 "small in build", 矮小的房子. It is the opposite of 高大. 矮 means short in height and is used for people, not for a short length of a thing (that's 短).
column4: 他的身材矮小，但是很有力气。
column5: 他的身材矮小，但是很有力氣。
column6: Tā de shēncái ǎixiǎo, dànshì hěn yǒu lìqi.
column7: He is small in build, but very strong.
column9: Short and small, for a person or a building, a little unflattering: 身材矮小 "small in build", 矮小的房子. It is the opposite of 高大. 矮 means short in height and is used for people, not for a short length of a thing (that's 短).

column3: Fat of animals and meat (肥肉 "fatty meat", 肥猪) and "loose, baggy" for clothes: 这条裤子太肥了. For people, 胖 is the neutral word; 肥 about a person is rude. It also means "fertile" and "fertilizer", as in 化肥. The flesh radical ⺼ is on the left.
column6: Zhè tiáo kùzi tài féi le.
column7: These trousers are too baggy.
column9: Fat of animals and meat (肥肉 "fatty meat", 肥豬) and "loose, baggy" for clothes: 這條褲子太肥了. For people, 胖 is the neutral word; 肥 about a person is rude. It also means "fertile" and "fertilizer", as in 化肥. The flesh radical ⺼ is on the left.

column3: Weak: 身体弱 "weak in health", 弱点 "weak point", 弱者 "the weak". Opposite of 强. After a number it means "a little under": 三分之一弱. The character is two bows 弓, each with two small marks; it just helps to see it as a double.
column6: Tā shēntǐ hěn ruò, jīngcháng shēngbìng.
column7: She is physically weak and often ill.
column9: Weak: 身體弱 "weak in health", 弱點 "weak point", 弱者 "the weak". Opposite of 強. After a number it means "a little under": 三分之一弱. The character is two bows 弓, each with two small marks; it just helps to see it as a double.

column3: To have a fever: 发烧了, 发高烧 "have a high fever". A verb and its object, so the 了 goes after: 发烧了. 发 is "to give out", 烧 "burn", so the body gives off heat. Slang 发烧友 is a "fan, buff", as in an audio buff.
column6: Háizi fāshāo le, yào qù yīyuàn.
column7: The child has a fever and needs to go to the hospital.
column9: To have a fever: 發燒了, 發高燒 "have a high fever". A verb and its object, so the 了 goes after: 發燒了. 發 is "to give out", 燒 "burn", so the body gives off heat. Slang 發燒友 is a "fan, buff", as in an audio buff.

column3: Nausea; to feel sick, or "disgusting": 我觉得恶心 "I feel sick", 太恶心了 "so gross". The reading is ě, not è as in 恶 "evil".
column6: Wǒ zuò chuán huì juéde ěxīn.
column7: I feel sick when I take a boat.
column9: Nausea; to feel sick, or "disgusting": 我覺得噁心 "I feel sick", 太噁心了 "so gross". The reading is ě, not è as in 惡 "evil".

column3: To get or give an injection: 去打针, 打了一针. In Chinese you "hit" a needle with 打, as with 打电话. The needle is 针, and it also counts the shots: 打一针. Past tense: 打了针 or 打了一针.
column6: Háizi zuì pà dǎzhēn.
column7: Children are most afraid of injections.
column9: To get or give an injection: 去打針, 打了一針. In Chinese you "hit" a needle with 打, as with 打電話. The needle is 針, and it also counts the shots: 打一針. Past tense: 打了針 or 打了一針.

column3: An "operation" or surgery: 做手术 is used both for the surgeon and the patient: 医生给他做手术, 他做了手术. 动手术 is another way to say it. 手 is "hand" and 术 "skill", so surgery is "work by hand".
column6: Tā xià zhōu yào zuò shǒushù.
column7: He is having an operation next week.
column9: An "operation" or surgery: 做手術 is used both for the surgeon and the patient: 醫生給他做手術, 他做了手術. 動手術 is another way to say it. 手 is "hand" and 術 "skill", so surgery is "work by hand".

column3: To treat a disease and cure it: 治病 "treat illness", 治好了 "cured", 很难治. It also means "to govern" in 治国 and "to manage" in 治理. It is often met in compounds such as 治疗.
column6: Zhè zhǒng bìng hěn nán zhì.
column7: This illness is hard to cure.
column9: To treat a disease and cure it: 治病 "treat illness", 治好了 "cured", 很難治. It also means "to govern" in 治國 and "to manage" in 治理. It is often met in compounds such as 治療.

column3: To treat an illness, or "treatment": 接受治疗 "receive treatment", 治疗方法 "method of treatment". It is the formal word for the doctor's work. 疗 has 疒 "sickness" under which the cure is written.
column6: Tā zhèngzài yīyuàn jiēshòu zhìliáo.
column7: He is receiving treatment at the hospital.
column9: To treat an illness, or "treatment": 接受治療 "receive treatment", 治療方法 "method of treatment". It is the formal word for the doctor's work. 療 has 疒 "sickness" under which the cure is written.

column3: Medical care, medical treatment: 医疗条件 "medical facilities", 医疗保险 "health insurance", 医疗费用 "medical costs". It names the system and services as a whole, not an individual act; for that use 治疗.
column6: Zhèlǐ de yīliáo tiáojiàn hěn hǎo.
column7: The medical facilities here are very good.
column9: Medical care, medical treatment: 醫療條件 "medical facilities", 醫療保險 "health insurance", 醫療費用 "medical costs". It names the system and services as a whole, not an individual act; for that use 治療.

column3: Medicine as a science or subject of study: 学医学, 医学院 "medical school", 医学研究. It is not the word for medicine you take; that is 药. 医 is "medical", 学 "study". Compare 医生 "doctor".
column6: Tā zài dàxué xuéxí yīxué.
column7: She studies medicine at university.
column9: Medicine as a science or subject of study: 學醫學, 醫學院 "medical school", 醫學研究. It is not the word for medicine you take; that is 藥. 醫 is "medical", 學 "study". Compare 醫生 "doctor".

column3: Internal medicine, the department of a hospital for illnesses treated without surgery: 内科医生, 挂内科. Its opposite is 外科 "surgery". 内 is "inside" and 科 "department, branch". You may be sent to 内科 for stomach or heart trouble.
column6: Qǐngwèn nèikē zài jǐ lóu?
column7: Excuse me, which floor is internal medicine on?
column9: Internal medicine, the department of a hospital for illnesses treated without surgery: 內科醫生, 掛內科. Its opposite is 外科 "surgery". 內 is "inside" and 科 "department, branch". You may be sent to 內科 for stomach or heart trouble.

column3: A "nurse": 护士小姐, 当护士. The 士 is neutral here (hùshi), unlike the full-tone 士 of 男士 and 女士. 护 is "to protect", with 扌 "hand" and 户 "door" for the sound, and 士 marks a person with a skill. A male nurse is 男护士.
column6: Hùshi gěi wǒ liáng le tǐwēn.
column7: The nurse took my temperature.
column9: A "nurse": 護士小姐, 當護士. The 士 is neutral here (hùshi), unlike the full-tone 士 of 男士 and 女士. 護 is "to protect", with 言 "speech" and 蒦 for the sound, and 士 marks a person with a skill. A male nurse is 男護士.

column3: Medication, drugs, a formal word for medicines taken as a group: 药物治疗 "drug treatment", 药物过敏 "drug allergy". In speech, 药 is enough. 药 has 艹 "plant" on top, as many were once herbs.
column4: 这种药物有一些副作用。
column5: 這種藥物有一些副作用。
column6: Zhè zhǒng yàowù yǒu yīxiē fùzuòyòng.
column7: This medication has some side effects.
column9: Medication, drugs, a formal word for medicines taken as a group: 藥物治療 "drug treatment", 藥物過敏 "drug allergy". In speech, 藥 is enough. 藥 has 艹 "plant" on top, as many were once herbs.

column3: A "physical examination, check-up": 做体检, 去体检, 体检报告. Companies and schools arrange it every year. It is short for 体格检查 "physical examination". 检 is "to check".
column4: 公司每年都让我们做体检。
column5: 公司每年都讓我們做體檢。
column6: Gōngsī měi nián dōu ràng wǒmen zuò tǐjiǎn.
column7: The company has us do a medical check-up every year.
column9: A "physical examination, check-up": 做體檢, 去體檢, 體檢報告. Companies and schools arrange it every year. It is short for 體格檢查 "physical examination". 檢 is "to check".

column3: To convalesce, recuperate, a stay at a rest home or in the mountains or by the sea to get well: 疗养院 "sanatorium". It is for a long-term recovery or a break for one's health. 疗 is "cure", 养 "nourish, raise".
column4: 他在海边疗养了一个月。
column5: 他在海邊療養了一個月。
column6: Tā zài hǎibiān liáoyǎng le yī ge yuè.
column7: He recovered by the sea for a month.
column9: To convalesce, recuperate, a stay at a rest home or in the mountains or by the sea to get well: 療養院 "sanatorium". It is for a long-term recovery or a break for one's health. 療 is "cure", 養 "nourish, raise".

column3: To lose weight, go on a diet: 想减肥, 在减肥. A verb and its object (减 "reduce", 肥 "fat"), so you say 减肥了 for "has started a diet", and 瘦了五公斤 "lost five kilos" for the result.
column4: 她最近在减肥，不吃晚饭。
column5: 她最近在減肥，不吃晚飯。
column6: Tā zuìjìn zài jiǎnféi, bù chī wǎnfàn.
column7: She is on a diet lately and skips dinner.
column9: To lose weight, go on a diet: 想減肥, 在減肥. A verb and its object (減 "reduce", 肥 "fat"), so you say 減肥了 for "has started a diet", and 瘦了五公斤 "lost five kilos" for the result.

column3: To ease, relieve: 缓解压力 "relieve stress", 缓解疼痛 "ease pain", 缓解交通 "ease traffic". It refers to a problem becoming less severe, not solved. 缓 means "slow", 解 "to untie, to loosen".
column6: Tīng yīnyuè kěyǐ huǎnjiě yālì.
column7: Listening to music can relieve stress.
column9: To ease, relieve: 緩解壓力 "relieve stress", 緩解疼痛 "ease pain", 緩解交通 "ease traffic". It refers to a problem becoming less severe, not solved. 緩 means "slow", 解 "to untie, to loosen".

column3: To harm, hurt, physically or emotionally: 伤害别人, 伤害感情 "hurt feelings", 受到伤害. Both characters mean "hurt" and make a formal verb. It does not mean to get injured by accident; that is 受伤.
column6: Bùyào shānghài biérén de gǎnqíng.
column7: Don't hurt other people's feelings.
column9: To harm, hurt, physically or emotionally: 傷害別人, 傷害感情 "hurt feelings", 受到傷害. Both characters mean "hurt" and make a formal verb. It does not mean to get injured by accident; that is 受傷.

column3: A "needle, pin": 一根针, 缝衣针, 针线 "needle and thread". Also "injection" (打针) and "stitch". 针灸 is acupuncture. 钅 is the metal radical and 十 gives the shape of a pin.
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī gēn zhēn.
column7: Please give me a needle.
column9: A "needle, pin": 一根針, 縫衣針, 針線 "needle and thread". Also "injection" (打針) and "stitch". 針灸 is acupuncture. 釒 is the metal radical and 十 gives the shape of a pin.

column3: An "alarm clock": 设闹钟 or 定闹钟 "set an alarm", 闹钟响了 "the alarm went off". In most homes it is a phone alarm now. 闹 means "noisy" and is a gate 门 over a market 市; 钟 is "clock".
column6: Wǒ bǎ nàozhōng dìng zài liù diǎn.
column7: I set the alarm for six o'clock.
column9: An "alarm clock": 設鬧鐘 or 定鬧鐘 "set an alarm", 鬧鐘響了 "the alarm went off". In most homes it is a phone alarm now. 鬧 means "noisy" and is 鬥 around a market 市; 鐘 is "clock".

column3: To wake up, or to be awake: 醒了 "woke up", 醒来 "wake up", 睡醒 "wake from sleep". It is not the word for getting out of bed, which is 起床. The wine jar 酉 shows that it also means "sobering up".
column6: Wǒ jīntiān liù diǎn jiù xǐng le.
column7: I woke up already at six today.
column9: To wake up, or to be awake: 醒了 "woke up", 醒來 "wake up", 睡醒 "wake from sleep". It is not the word for getting out of bed, which is 起床. The wine jar 酉 shows that it also means "sobering up".

column3: Clear-headed, awake, sober: 头脑清醒 "clear-headed", 清醒过来 "come to". It means the mind is clear, after sleep, after drinking or after a faint. 清 is "clear" and 醒 "awake". Opposite of 糊涂 or 昏迷.
column6: Hē le kāfēi, wǒ qīngxǐng duō le.
column7: After the coffee I am much more awake.
column9: Clear-headed, awake, sober: 頭腦清醒 "clear-headed", 清醒過來 "come to". It means the mind is clear, after sleep, after drinking or after a faint. 清 is "clear" and 醒 "awake". Opposite of 糊塗 or 昏迷.

column3: This reading is a complement of success or contact: 睡着 "fall asleep", 找着 "find", 着火 "catch fire", 着凉 "catch a cold". It is the same character as the particle 着 (zhe), as in 坐着, but here it is read zháo.
column6: Zuówǎn wǒ yīzhí shuì bù zháo.
column7: Last night I couldn't fall asleep at all.
column9: This reading is a complement of success or contact: 睡著 "fall asleep", 找著 "find", 著火 "catch fire", 著涼 "catch a cold". It is the same character as the particle 著 (zhe), as in 坐著, but here it is read zháo.

column3: To fall asleep: 睡着了, 睡不着 "can't fall asleep". 睡 is the sleeping and 着 (zháo) shows it has been reached. 睡觉 is to sleep, 睡着 is to actually drop off: 我躺了一个小时才睡着. 睡 has 目 "eye" with 垂 "droop".
column6: Háizi yǐjīng shuìzháo le.
column7: The child has already fallen asleep.
column9: To fall asleep: 睡著了, 睡不著 "can't fall asleep". 睡 is the sleeping and 著 (zháo) shows it has been reached. 睡覺 is to sleep, 睡著 is to actually drop off: 我躺了一個小時才睡著. 睡 has 目 "eye" with 垂 "droop".

column3: To lie down, recline: 躺在床上, 躺下. 躺下 is "lie down", and 躺着 "lying". 躺 has 身 "body" on the left and 尚, which gives the sound.
column6: Tā tǎng zài shāfā shàng kàn diànshì.
column7: He is lying on the sofa watching TV.
column9: To lie down, recline: 躺在床上, 躺下. 躺下 is "lie down", and 躺著 "lying". 躺 has 身 "body" on the left and 尚, which gives the sound.

column3: A "dream" in sleep, and also a hope: 做梦 "dream", 一个梦, 梦想 "dream, ambition". The character puts 林 "woods" over 夕 "evening" and one way to read it is two closed eyes at night.
column6: Wǒ zuówǎn zuò le yī ge hǎo mèng.
column7: I had a good dream last night.
column9: A "dream" in sleep, and also a hope: 做夢 "dream", 一個夢, 夢想 "dream, ambition". The character puts 艹, 罒 and 冖 over 夕 "evening" and one way to read it is two closed eyes at night.

column3: To dream of someone or something: 梦见了她, 梦见自己飞 "dream of flying". 见 is a result complement showing you saw it. You dream about the thing directly, with no preposition: 我梦见你了. Compare 做梦 "to have a dream".
column4: 我昨天梦见了我的奶奶。
column5: 我昨天夢見了我的奶奶。
column6: Wǒ zuótiān mèngjiàn le wǒ de nǎinai.
column7: Yesterday I dreamed about my grandmother.
column9: To dream of someone or something: 夢見了她, 夢見自己飛 "dream of flying". 見 is a result complement showing you saw it. You dream about the thing directly, with no preposition: 我夢見你了. Compare 做夢 "to have a dream".

column3: To dream, a verb and its object, so other words can go between: 做了一个梦. Figuratively "to daydream, to dream on", often scornful: 你做梦吧！ "In your dreams!" and 做梦都想… "to dream of … even in sleep", a way to say you want something badly.
column6: Tā zuòmèng dōu xiǎng dāng yīshēng.
column7: He dreams of becoming a doctor, even in his sleep.
column9: To dream, a verb and its object, so other words can go between: 做了一個夢. Figuratively "to daydream, to dream on", often scornful: 你做夢吧！ "In your dreams!" and 做夢都想… "to dream of … even in sleep", a way to say you want something badly.

column3: To brush one's teeth: 刷牙, 刷了牙. A verb and its object (刷 "brush", 牙 "tooth"), so 我每天刷两次牙, with the number between. The toothbrush is 牙刷.
column6: Shuìjiào qián yào shuāyá.
column7: You must brush your teeth before going to bed.
column9: To brush one's teeth: 刷牙, 刷了牙. A verb and its object (刷 "brush", 牙 "tooth"), so 我每天刷兩次牙, with the number between. The toothbrush is 牙刷.

column3: A "toothbrush": 一把牙刷. It is 刷牙 in reverse: 牙刷 is the thing and 刷牙 the action. Toothpaste is 牙膏. The measure word is 把 for brushes.
column6: Wǒ wàng le dài yáshuā.
column7: I forgot to bring a toothbrush.
column9: A "toothbrush": 一把牙刷. It is 刷牙 in reverse: 牙刷 is the thing and 刷牙 the action. Toothpaste is 牙膏. The measure word is 把 for brushes.

column3: A "towel": 一条毛巾, 擦脸的毛巾. 毛 is "fur, hair", which is the soft nap of a towel, and 巾 is a hanging cloth. A bath towel is 浴巾; 毛巾 is the smaller face or hand towel.
column4: 请给我一条干净的毛巾。
column5: 請給我一條乾淨的毛巾。
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī tiáo gānjìng de máojīn.
column7: Please give me a clean towel.
column9: A "towel": 一條毛巾, 擦臉的毛巾. 毛 is "fur, hair", which is the soft nap of a towel, and 巾 is a hanging cloth. A bath towel is 浴巾; 毛巾 is the smaller face or hand towel.

column3: To brush, scrub: 刷牙, 刷碗 "wash dishes", 刷鞋. Also "to swipe" a card (刷卡 "pay by card") and "to scroll" a screen (刷手机). The character has a knife radical 刂 on the right.
column6: Chīwán fàn, wǒ lái shuā wǎn.
column7: After the meal I'll wash the dishes.
column9: To brush, scrub: 刷牙, 刷碗 "wash dishes", 刷鞋. Also "to swipe" a card (刷卡 "pay by card") and "to scroll" a screen (刷手機). The character has a knife radical 刂 on the right.

column3: A "brush" for scrubbing or painting: 一把刷子, 鞋刷子, 刷子刷鞋. The brush is a thing, 刷 the action. The 子 is neutral. A toothbrush is called 牙刷 rather than 牙刷子.
column6: Yòng shuāzi xǐ bēizi.
column7: Wash the cups with a brush.
column9: A "brush" for scrubbing or painting: 一把刷子, 鞋刷子, 刷子刷鞋. The brush is a thing, 刷 the action. The 子 is neutral. A toothbrush is called 牙刷 rather than 牙刷子.

column3: To smoke a cigarette: 抽烟, 不抽烟 "I don't smoke", 禁止抽烟 "no smoking". 抽 is "to draw out, pull" and 烟 "smoke" or "tobacco". It is the usual spoken verb; 吸烟 sounds more formal.
column6: Qǐng bùyào zài zhèlǐ chōuyān.
column7: Please don't smoke here.
column9: To smoke a cigarette: 抽煙, 不抽煙 "I don't smoke", 禁止抽煙 "no smoking". 抽 is "to draw out, pull" and 煙 "smoke" or "tobacco". It is the usual spoken verb; 吸煙 sounds more formal.
