column9: Behind, at the back: 後 "back" plus 頭 "end". Spoken, with a neutral second syllable (hòutou). Place: 站在我後頭; time: "later, afterwards": 後頭再說. The written form is 後面.

column3: On the stage, on the platform: 台 "platform" plus 上 "on". 台上的人 "the people on stage". It is the place word for 台 plus 上: use 台下 for "in the audience".
column6: Tā zhàn zài táishàng jiǎnghuà.
column7: He stands on the stage and speaks.
column9: On the stage, on the platform: 臺 "platform" plus 上 "on". 臺上的人 "the people on stage". It is the place word for 臺 plus 上: use 臺下 for "in the audience".

column3: In one's hands: 手 "hand" plus 里 "inside". It is a place phrase with a person before it: 他手里有一本书. It can also mean "in someone's control": 钱在他手里. Spoken.
column6: Tā shǒulǐ názhe yī běn shū.
column7: He is holding a book in his hands.
column9: In one's hands: 手 "hand" plus 裡 "inside". It is a place phrase with a person before it: 他手裡有一本書. It can also mean "in someone's control": 錢在他手裡. Spoken.

column3: In the eyes: 眼 "eye" plus 里 "inside". A place phrase: 眼里都是泪水 "eyes full of tears". Figuratively: 他眼里只有工作 "he has eyes only for work". The 里 is neutral in speech (yǎnli). 眼 has 目 for the eye and 艮 for the sound.
column6: Tā yǎnli dōu shì lèishuǐ.
column7: Her eyes are full of tears.
column9: In the eyes: 眼 "eye" plus 裡 "inside". A place phrase: 眼裡都是淚水 "eyes full of tears". Figuratively: 他眼裡只有工作 "he has eyes only for work". The 裡 is neutral in speech (yǎnli). 眼 has 目 for the eye and 艮 for the sound.

column3: Both sides: 两 "two" plus 边 "side". Used for a street, a river, a face: 路的两边, 左右两边. Without a measure word. Also, the two parties of a matter: 两边都有道理. 边 is 辶 with 力.
column6: Lù de liǎngbiān dōu yǒu shù.
column7: There are trees on both sides of the road.
column9: Both sides: 兩 "two" plus 邊 "side". Used for a street, a river, a face: 路的兩邊, 左右兩邊. Without a measure word. Also, the two parties of a matter: 兩邊都有道理. 邊 is 辶 with 臱.

column3: Bottom, base: 海底 "sea floor", 鞋底 "sole", 底下 "underneath". Also "end of a period": 月底 "end of the month", 年底. Also "background" (底色). 底 has 广 "building" and 氐 as its sound.
column6: Bēizi de dǐ pò le.
column7: The bottom of the cup is broken.
column9: Bottom, base: 海底 "sea floor", 鞋底 "sole", 底下 "underneath". Also "end of a period": 月底 "end of the month", 年底. Also "background" (底色). 底 has 广 "building" and 氐 as its sound.

column3: End, tip: most often in 周末 "weekend", 月末 "end of the month", 期末. It is 木 with a stroke at the top, the tip of the tree, while 本 has it at the bottom, the root. After a time word it says "at the end of": 十月末.
column6: Tā zài shíyuè mò huíguó.
column7: He returns to his country at the end of October.
column9: End, tip: most often in 週末 "weekend", 月末 "end of the month", 期末. It is 木 with a stroke at the top, the tip of the tree, while 本 has it at the bottom, the root. After a time word it says "at the end of": 十月末.

column3: Measure word for places and points: 三处错误, 几处地方. Also bound: 好处 "benefit", 到处 "everywhere", 办事处 "office". Read chù as a noun. As a verb "to get along" (相处) or "to deal with" it is chǔ. 处 is 夂 and 卜.
column6: Zhèlǐ yǒu sān chù cuòwù.
column7: There are three mistakes here.
column9: Measure word for places and points: 三處錯誤, 幾處地方. Also bound: 好處 "benefit", 到處 "everywhere", 辦事處 "office". Read chù as a noun. As a verb "to get along" (相處) or "to deal with" it is chǔ. 處 has 虍, 夂 and 几.

column3: Position, place: 位 "place" plus 置 "put". Where something is or sits: 座位的位置, 重要的位置. A person's position in a ranking or social setting too. The second syllable is neutral in speech (wèizhi). 位 shows 亻 beside 立 "stand".
column6: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de wèizhi.
column7: Please tell me where you are.
column9: Position, place: 位 "place" plus 置 "put". Where something is or sits: 座位的位置, 重要的位置. A person's position in a ranking or social setting too. The second syllable is neutral in speech (wèizhi). 位 shows 亻 beside 立 "stand".

column3: Inside, internal: 内 "inside" plus 部 "part". Of an organization or object: 公司内部, 内部结构. Often with a hint of "not for outsiders": 内部资料. Opposite 外部. 内 shows a person 人 entering a frame 冂.
column6: Gōngsī nèibù yǒu hěn duō guīdìng.
column7: There are many rules within the company.
column9: Inside, internal: 內 "inside" plus 部 "part". Of an organization or object: 公司內部, 內部結構. Often with a hint of "not for outsiders": 內部資料. Opposite 外部. 內 shows 入 entering a frame 冂.

column3: To separate, to be apart by: 我家和公司隔一条街, 隔天 "every other day", 隔壁 "next door". It shows a gap in space or time. The 阝 on the left means a wall or mound, and 鬲 gives the sound.
column6: Wǒ jiā hé gōngsī gé yī tiáo jiē.
column7: My home is one street away from the company.
column9: To separate, to be apart by: 我家和公司隔一條街, 隔天 "every other day", 隔壁 "next door". It shows a gap in space or time. The 阝 on the left means a wall or mound, and 鬲 gives the sound.

column3: To separate, to divide two things with something between: 隔 "separate" plus 开 "apart". A wall, a river or a curtain does the dividing: 用墙隔开, 隔开房间. The result complement 开 shows the parts are apart.
column4: 一堵墙把两个房间隔开了。
column5: 一堵牆把兩個房間隔開了。
column6: Yī dǔ qiáng bǎ liǎng ge fángjiān gékāi le.
column7: A wall separates the two rooms.
column9: To separate, to divide two things with something between: 隔 "separate" plus 開 "apart". A wall, a river or a curtain does the dividing: 用牆隔開, 隔開房間. The result complement 開 shows the parts are apart.

column3: Square, and a side or direction: 方形 "square shape", 地方 "place", 对方 "the other party", 方法 "method". As a plain adjective it means "square": 方桌. It also means "upright, honest" in 方正. Many compounds use 方.
column6: Zhège zhuōzi shì fāng de.
column7: This table is square.
column9: Square, and a side or direction: 方形 "square shape", 地方 "place", 對方 "the other party", 方法 "method". As a plain adjective it means "square": 方桌. It also means "upright, honest" in 方正. Many compounds use 方.

column3: Distance: 距 "be apart from" plus 离 "leave". Between two places or times: 距离学校很近, 保持距离. It works as a noun (一段距离) and as a preposition-like verb (我家距离学校很近). 距 has 足 "foot" and 巨 for sound.
column6: Wǒ jiā jùlí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
column7: My home is very close to the school.
column9: Distance: 距 "be apart from" plus 離 "leave". Between two places or times: 距離學校很近, 保持距離. It works as a noun (一段距離) and as a preposition-like verb (我家距離學校很近). 距 has 足 "foot" and 巨 for sound.

column3: Space, room: 空 "empty" plus 间 "gap". Physical space (空间太小) and room to grow (发展空间), and in physics and astronomy. Not "room" as in a bedroom: for that use 房间. 空 has 穴 "cave" and 工 for sound.
column4: 这个房间的空间太小了。
column5: 這個房間的空間太小了。
column6: Zhège fángjiān de kōngjiān tài xiǎo le.
column7: The space in this room is too small.
column9: Space, room: 空 "empty" plus 間 "gap". Physical space (空間太小) and room to grow (發展空間), and in physics and astronomy. Not "room" as in a bedroom: for that use 房間. 空 has 穴 "cave" and 工 for sound.

column3: Here kòng, "free time, spare": 有空 "have time", 没空, 空儿 "spare moment". It is a different reading from kōng "empty, sky". The pattern: 你有空吗? is how you ask if someone is free. 空 has 穴 "cave" on top; a cave is empty.
column6: Nǐ míngtiān yǒu kòng ma?
column7: Are you free tomorrow?
column9: Here kòng, "free time, spare": 有空 "have time", 沒空, 空兒 "spare moment". It is a different reading from kōng "empty, sky". The pattern: 你有空嗎? is how you ask if someone is free. 空 has 穴 "cave" on top; a cave is empty.

column3: Moved, excited, stirred up by strong emotion, good or bad: 激 "stir" plus 动 "move". 听到消息很激动; 激动得哭了 "so moved that he cried". It is about being emotionally shaken, tearful or trembling, and need not be happy. 兴奋 is plain excitement.
column4: 听到这个消息，他很激动。
column5: 聽到這個消息，他很激動。
column6: Tīng dào zhège xiāoxi, tā hěn jīdòng.
column7: Hearing the news, he was very moved.
column9: Moved, excited, stirred up by strong emotion, good or bad: 激 "stir" plus 動 "move". 聽到消息很激動; 激動得哭了 "so moved that he cried". It is about being emotionally shaken, tearful or trembling, and need not be happy. 興奮 is plain excitement.

column3: Excited, thrilled: 兴 "joy" plus 奋 "rouse". A happy, energetic state: 兴奋得睡不着 "too excited to sleep". The 兴 here is xīng, as in 高兴 and 兴奋; the xìng of 兴趣 is a different reading. 奋 has 大 "big" over 田 "field".
column4: 孩子们兴奋地跑了出来。
column5: 孩子們興奮地跑了出來。
column6: Háizimen xīngfèn de pǎo le chūlái.
column7: The children ran out excitedly.
column9: Excited, thrilled: 興 "joy" plus 奮 "rouse". A happy, energetic state: 興奮得睡不著 "too excited to sleep". The 興 here is xīng, as in 高興 and 興奮; the xìng of 興趣 is a different reading. 奮 has 大 "big" over 田 "field".

column3: Disappointed, to lose hope: 失 "lose" plus 望 "hope". A feeling after something has not turned out as hoped: 很失望, 对…失望, 让人失望. The object comes with 对: 我对他很失望. 望 combines 王 with 月: gazing at the moon.
column6: Kǎoshì méi guò, wǒ hěn shīwàng.
column7: I failed the exam and am very disappointed.
column9: Disappointed, to lose hope: 失 "lose" plus 望 "hope". A feeling after something has not turned out as hoped: 很失望, 對…失望, 讓人失望. The object comes with 對: 我對他很失望. 望 combines 王 with 月: gazing at the moon.

column3: To be startled, to be shocked: 吃 "take in" plus 惊 "fright". Verb-object: 吃了一惊, 大吃一惊 "gave a great start". The cause goes before: 听到…很吃惊. Surprise, not fear. 惊 has 忄 "heart" and 京 as the sound.
column4: 听到他结婚了，我很吃惊。
column5: 聽到他結婚了，我很吃驚。
column6: Tīng dào tā jiéhūn le, wǒ hěn chījīng.
column7: I was shocked to hear he got married.
column9: To be startled, to be shocked: 吃 "take in" plus 驚 "fright". Verb-object: 吃了一驚, 大吃一驚 "gave a great start". The cause goes before: 聽到…很吃驚. Surprise, not fear. 驚 has 馬 and 敬 as the sound.

column3: Delighted, to one's heart's content: 痛 "keenly" plus 快 "fast". Used for a release of feeling after something satisfying: 玩得很痛快, 说话痛快 "speaks frankly". 痛 has 疒 "sickness" for pain.
column6: Xǐ le ge rè shuǐzǎo, zhēn tòngkuài.
column7: A hot bath: how satisfying!
column9: Delighted, to one's heart's content: 痛 "keenly" plus 快 "fast". Used for a release of feeling after something satisfying: 玩得很痛快, 說話痛快 "speaks frankly". 痛 has 疒 "sickness" for pain.

column3: Pleased with oneself, proud: 得 "get" plus 意 "intention". Often a bit negative, as in smug: 得意洋洋 "swaggering". It describes a feeling after succeeding, or after a stroke of luck. 意 has 音 "sound" over 心 "heart": what is in your heart.
column6: Tā kǎo le dì yī míng, hěn déyì.
column7: He came first in the exam and is very pleased with himself.
column9: Pleased with oneself, proud: 得 "get" plus 意 "intention". Often a bit negative, as in smug: 得意洋洋 "swaggering". It describes a feeling after succeeding, or after a stroke of luck. 意 has 音 "sound" over 心 "heart": what is in your heart.

column3: Annoyed, to bother: 别烦我 "don't bother me", 烦死了 "so annoying", 心烦 "upset". Also "tedious": 麻烦. It is the basic word in 烦恼 and 麻烦. 烦 has 火 "fire", for a burning mood, and 页 "head".
column6: Bié fán wǒ, wǒ zài gōngzuò.
column7: Don't bother me; I am working.
column9: Annoyed, to bother: 別煩我 "don't bother me", 煩死了 "so annoying", 心煩 "upset". Also "tedious": 麻煩. It is the basic word in 煩惱 and 麻煩. 煩 has 火 "fire", for a burning mood, and 頁 "head".

column3: To worry, to be anxious, usually about time: 着 "touch" plus 急 "urgent". The first syllable is zháo here, not zhe. 别着急 "don't worry, take your time" is the phrase you meet most. It is about hurry and pressure rather than fear.
column6: Bié zháojí, mànmàn shuō.
column7: Don't worry, speak slowly.
column9: To worry, to be anxious, usually about time: 著 "touch" plus 急 "urgent". The first syllable is zháo here, not zhe. 別著急 "don't worry, take your time" is the phrase you meet most. It is about hurry and pressure rather than fear.

column3: To worry: 担 "bear" plus 心 "heart". Verb-object, but the object can follow: 担心你, 担心他的健康; 别担心. It is about something that may go wrong. 担 has 扌 "hand" because it first meant to carry on the shoulder.
column6: Māma hěn dānxīn nǐ.
column7: Mom worries a lot about you.
column9: To worry: 擔 "bear" plus 心 "heart". Verb-object, but the object can follow: 擔心你, 擔心他的健康; 別擔心. It is about something that may go wrong. 擔 has 扌 "hand" because it first meant to carry on the shoulder.

column3: To cherish the memory of, to look back fondly: 怀 "bosom" plus 念 "think of". The object is a past, a person who is gone or a time: 怀念童年, 怀念老朋友. It is for what is lost or far away in time. 想念 is for someone you can still see.
column4: 我很怀念小时候的生活。
column5: 我很懷念小時候的生活。
column6: Wǒ hěn huáiniàn xiǎoshíhou de shēnghuó.
column7: I fondly remember life when I was little.
column9: To cherish the memory of, to look back fondly: 懷 "bosom" plus 念 "think of". The object is a past, a person who is gone or a time: 懷念童年, 懷念老朋友. It is for what is lost or far away in time. 想念 is for someone you can still see.

column3: To miss someone or somewhere: 想 "think" plus 念 "miss". Typical object: a person or home: 想念家人, 想念你. It is warm and works in letters and messages. For the past, rather than present absence, 怀念. 念 is 今 over 心: "the present on the mind".
column6: Wǒ hěn xiǎngniàn wǒ de jiārén.
column7: I miss my family very much.
column9: To miss someone or somewhere: 想 "think" plus 念 "miss". Typical object: a person or home: 想念家人, 想念你. It is warm and works in letters and messages. For the past, rather than present absence, 懷念. 念 is 今 over 心: "the present on the mind".

column3: To sympathize, sympathy: 同 "same" plus 情 "feeling". You feel it for someone who is badly off: 同情他, 同情的目光. Sometimes mixed with pity, so it is not always welcome. For agreeing with someone, use 同意 or 赞成.
column6: Dàjiā dōu hěn tóngqíng tā.
column7: Everyone feels sorry for him.
column9: To sympathize, sympathy: 同 "same" plus 情 "feeling". You feel it for someone who is badly off: 同情他, 同情的目光. Sometimes mixed with pity, so it is not always welcome. For agreeing with someone, use 同意 or 贊成.

column3: To look forward to: 期 "expect" plus 待 "wait". The object is an event or news: 期待你的来信, 期待见面. Also a noun, "expectation": 不负期待. More formal than 盼 and 等. 待 has 彳 "step" and 寺 for sound.
column6: Wǒ qīdài nǐ de láixìn.
column7: I look forward to your letter.
column9: To look forward to: 期 "expect" plus 待 "wait". The object is an event or news: 期待你的來信, 期待見面. Also a noun, "expectation": 不負期待. More formal than 盼 and 等. 待 has 彳 "step" and 寺 for sound.

column3: To doubt, to suspect: 怀 "harbor" plus 疑 "doubt". It takes a clause: 我怀疑他在说谎 "I suspect he is lying". It often means "suspect that" rather than "doubt that": 怀疑他不来 means "I suspect he's not coming". 怀 is 忄 "heart" beside 不.
column6: Wǒ huáiyí tā zài shuōhuǎng.
column7: I suspect he is lying.
column9: To doubt, to suspect: 懷 "harbor" plus 疑 "doubt". It takes a clause: 我懷疑他在說謊 "I suspect he is lying". It often means "suspect that" rather than "doubt that": 懷疑他不來 means "I suspect he's not coming". 懷 is 忄 "heart" beside 褱.

column3: Urgent, pressing: 迫 "press" plus 切 "keen". Used for needs, wishes or tasks, and nearly always before a noun or 地 plus verb: 迫切的需要, 迫切地希望. More formal than 着急. 切 here is qiè; as "to cut" it is qiē.
column4: 我们迫切需要你的帮助。
column5: 我們迫切需要你的幫助。
column6: Wǒmen pòqiè xūyào nǐ de bāngzhù.
column7: We urgently need your help.
column9: Urgent, pressing: 迫 "press" plus 切 "keen". Used for needs, wishes or tasks, and nearly always before a noun or 地 plus verb: 迫切的需要, 迫切地希望. More formal than 著急. 切 here is qiè; as "to cut" it is qiē.

column3: Tranquil, peaceful and quiet: 宁 "calm" plus 静 "still". Used for places and states of mind: 宁静的夜晚, 内心宁静. A literary word, more poetic than 安静.
column6: Yèwǎn de cūnzi hěn níngjìng.
column7: The village is very peaceful at night.
column9: Tranquil, peaceful and quiet: 寧 "calm" plus 靜 "still". Used for places and states of mind: 寧靜的夜晚, 內心寧靜. A literary word, more poetic than 安靜.

column3: Calm, quiet: 平 "level" plus 静 "still". Of the sea, of a mood or of a life: 平静的湖面, 心情平静, 平静下来 "calm down". Without ripples; where 宁静 describes a scene, 平静 is the absence of agitation. 平 is a symbol of a level scale.
column6: Húmiàn hěn píngjìng.
column7: The surface of the lake is very calm.
column9: Calm, quiet: 平 "level" plus 靜 "still". Of the sea, of a mood or of a life: 平靜的湖面, 心情平靜, 平靜下來 "calm down". Without ripples; where 寧靜 describes a scene, 平靜 is the absence of agitation. 平 is a symbol of a level scale.

column3: Bored, boring: 无 "without" plus 聊 "something to rely on". Both for a person who is bored (我很无聊) and a thing that is dull (这部电影很无聊). 聊 alone means "to chat", as in 聊天.
column4: 周末一个人在家很无聊。
column5: 週末一個人在家很無聊。
column6: Zhōumò yī ge rén zài jiā hěn wúliáo.
column7: It is boring to be home alone at the weekend.
column9: Bored, boring: 無 "without" plus 聊 "something to rely on". Both for a person who is bored (我很無聊) and a thing that is dull (這部電影很無聊). 聊 alone means "to chat", as in 聊天.

column3: To be interested (in): 感 "feel" plus 兴趣 "interest". The thing goes after 对: 对…感兴趣, and the degree before 感: 很感兴趣, 不感兴趣. The 兴 is xìng here. You cannot say 感兴趣 + object directly.
column4: 我对中国历史很感兴趣。
column5: 我對中國歷史很感興趣。
column6: Wǒ duì Zhōngguó lìshǐ hěn gǎnxìngqù.
column7: I am very interested in Chinese history.
column9: To be interested (in): 感 "feel" plus 興趣 "interest". The thing goes after 對: 對…感興趣, and the degree before 感: 很感興趣, 不感興趣. The 興 is xìng here. You cannot say 感興趣 + object directly.

column3: Interest, hobby: 兴 "excitement" plus 趣 "fun". Read xìng here. Patterns: 对…有兴趣, 兴趣爱好 "hobbies", 培养兴趣 "cultivate an interest". 兴 is xīng in 高兴 "happy"; the two readings go with the two meanings.
column6: Nǐ yǒu shénme xìngqù àihào?
column7: What are your hobbies and interests?
column9: Interest, hobby: 興 "excitement" plus 趣 "fun". Read xìng here. Patterns: 對…有興趣, 興趣愛好 "hobbies", 培養興趣 "cultivate an interest". 興 is xīng in 高興 "happy"; the two readings go with the two meanings.

column3: Delight, joy found in something: 乐 "happy" plus 趣 "fun". A pleasure that comes from doing something: 生活的乐趣, 享受乐趣. The 乐 is lè "joy" here, not yuè "music". 趣 has 走 "walk" and 取: heading for what attracts.
column4: 读书给我带来很多乐趣。
column5: 讀書給我帶來很多樂趣。
column6: Dúshū gěi wǒ dàilái hěn duō lèqù.
column7: Reading brings me a lot of pleasure.
column9: Delight, joy found in something: 樂 "happy" plus 趣 "fun". A pleasure that comes from doing something: 生活的樂趣, 享受樂趣. The 樂 is lè "joy" here, not yuè "music". 趣 has 走 "walk" and 取: heading for what attracts.

column3: Interesting, amusing: 有 "have" plus 趣 "fun". Of a person, thing or story: 很有趣, 有趣的故事. It means "fun to watch or hear", with a light, curious feel. Different from 有意思, which is more common in speech. 趣 shows you walking toward fun.
column6: Zhè běn shū hěn yǒuqù.
column7: This book is very interesting.
column9: Interesting, amusing: 有 "have" plus 趣 "fun". Of a person, thing or story: 很有趣, 有趣的故事. It means "fun to watch or hear", with a light, curious feel. Different from 有意思, which is more common in speech. 趣 shows you walking toward fun.

column3: Energetic, fun, interesting in speech: 有 "have" plus 劲儿 "energy". 玩游戏很有劲儿 means it is exciting. Also "strong": 他很有劲儿. The 儿 ending is northern; the last syllable is a retroflex: jìnr. The opposite is 没劲.
column6: Wán yóuxì hěn yǒujìnr.
column7: Playing the game is a lot of fun.
column9: Energetic, fun, interesting in speech: 有 "have" plus 勁兒 "energy". 玩遊戲很有勁兒 means it is exciting. Also "strong": 他很有勁兒. The 兒 ending is northern; the last syllable is a retroflex: jìnr. The opposite is 沒勁.

column3: Lively, bustling: 热 "hot" plus 闹 "noisy". Of a place or occasion full of people and sound: 街上很热闹, 热闹非凡. Positive: lively, not annoying. As a verb, 热闹一下 "liven things up". The second syllable is neutral in speech: rènao.
column4: 过年的时候，街上很热闹。
column5: 過年的時候，街上很熱鬧。
column6: Guònián de shíhou, jiē shàng hěn rènao.
column7: At New Year the street is very lively.
column9: Lively, bustling: 熱 "hot" plus 鬧 "noisy". Of a place or occasion full of people and sound: 街上很熱鬧, 熱鬧非凡. Positive: lively, not annoying. As a verb, 熱鬧一下 "liven things up". The second syllable is neutral in speech: rènao.

column3: To make noise, to cause trouble: 别闹了 "stop fooling around". Also "to have an attack of" (闹肚子 "have an upset stomach"), and in many verb uses 闹笑话 "make a fool of oneself". 闹 shows a market 市 in a gate 门, a noisy place.
column6: Bié nào le, wǒ zài xiě zuòyè.
column7: Stop making noise; I am doing my homework.
column9: To make noise, to cause trouble: 別鬧了 "stop fooling around". Also "to have an attack of" (鬧肚子 "have an upset stomach"), and in many verb uses 鬧笑話 "make a fool of oneself". 鬧 shows a market 市 inside 鬥, a noisy place.

column3: Luck: 运 "fortune" plus 气 "air, spirit". Good or bad: 运气好, 运气不好, 碰运气 "try one's luck". Always about chance outcomes. The second syllable is neutral in speech (yùnqi). Compare 幸运 "lucky" as an adjective.
column6: Jīntiān wǒ yùnqi hěn hǎo.
column7: I am very lucky today.
column9: Luck: 運 "fortune" plus 氣 "air, spirit". Good or bad: 運氣好, 運氣不好, 碰運氣 "try one's luck". Always about chance outcomes. The second syllable is neutral in speech (yùnqi). Compare 幸運 "lucky" as an adjective.

column3: Balloon: 气 "air" plus 球 "ball". The kind that you blow up: 吹气球, 红气球. 球 has 王 "jade" beside 求: a "ball" was first a kind of jade. The measure word is 个.
column4: 孩子手里拿着一个红气球。
column5: 孩子手裡拿著一個紅氣球。
column6: Háizi shǒulǐ názhe yī ge hóng qìqiú.
column7: The child is holding a red balloon.
column9: Balloon: 氣 "air" plus 球 "ball". The kind that you blow up: 吹氣球, 紅氣球. 球 has 王 "jade" beside 求: a "ball" was first a kind of jade. The measure word is 個.

column3: Honest, truthful: 诚 "sincere" plus 实 "real". About a person who does not lie or cheat: 诚实的孩子, 诚实回答. Both characters share the idea of what is true. 诚 has 讠 "speech" and 成 for sound, so "words that are complete". Close to 老实, but 诚实 stresses telling the truth.
column6: Tā shì yī ge chéngshí de háizi.
column7: He is an honest child.
column9: Honest, truthful: 誠 "sincere" plus 實 "real". About a person who does not lie or cheat: 誠實的孩子, 誠實回答. Both characters share the idea of what is true. 誠 has 言 "speech" and 成 for sound, so "words that are complete". Close to 老實, but 誠實 stresses telling the truth.

column3: Honest, well-behaved, simple: 老 "old, always" plus 实 "real". Said of someone plain and obedient, who does not play tricks: 老老实实 "honestly, steadily". Can have a hint of naivety or of being easily fooled. 老实说 means "to be honest". The last syllable is neutral: lǎoshi.
column6: Tā hěn lǎoshi, cóng bù shuōhuǎng.
column7: He is honest and never lies.
column9: Honest, well-behaved, simple: 老 "old, always" plus 實 "real". Said of someone plain and obedient, who does not play tricks: 老老實實 "honestly, steadily". Can have a hint of naivety or of being easily fooled. 老實說 means "to be honest". The last syllable is neutral: lǎoshi.

column3: Honesty and good faith: 诚 "sincere" plus 信 "trust". A written, abstract word about keeping promises and being reliable: 讲诚信, 诚信经营 "honest business". Used for businesses, institutions and people alike. 信 has 亻 beside 言 "word": a person's word.
column6: Zuò shēngyi yào jiǎng chéngxìn.
column7: Business needs honesty and good faith.
column9: Honesty and good faith: 誠 "sincere" plus 信 "trust". A written, abstract word about keeping promises and being reliable: 講誠信, 誠信經營 "honest business". Used for businesses, institutions and people alike. 信 has 亻 beside 言 "word": a person's word.

column3: Brave: 勇 "courage" plus 敢 "dare". Said of persons and acts: 勇敢的战士, 勇敢地面对. It stresses facing danger or difficulty. The 力 under 甬 in 勇 means strength. 敢 alone is the verb "to dare": 不敢.
column6: Tā shì yī ge yǒnggǎn de rén.
column7: He is a brave person.
column9: Brave: 勇 "courage" plus 敢 "dare". Said of persons and acts: 勇敢的戰士, 勇敢地面對. It stresses facing danger or difficulty. The 力 under 甬 in 勇 means strength. 敢 alone is the verb "to dare": 不敢.

column3: Courage: 勇 "brave" plus 气 "spirit". A noun: 有勇气, 鼓起勇气 "pluck up one's courage". Describes the inner quality; for the trait in a person use 勇敢.
column6: Tā yǒu shuō zhēnhuà de yǒngqì.
column7: She has the courage to tell the truth.
column9: Courage: 勇 "brave" plus 氣 "spirit". A noun: 有勇氣, 鼓起勇氣 "pluck up one's courage". Describes the inner quality; for the trait in a person use 勇敢.

column3: Kind-hearted, good: 善 "good" plus 良 "fine". A trait of character: 善良的人, 心地善良. It means a person with a good heart who does not wish others harm. Not about manners, rather about the heart. 善 has 羊, a sheep, a symbol of good.
column6: Tā shì yī ge shànliáng de nǚhái.
column7: She is a kind-hearted girl.
column9: Kind-hearted, good: 善 "good" plus 良 "fine". A trait of character: 善良的人, 心地善良. It means a person with a good heart who does not wish others harm. Not about manners, rather about the heart. 善 has 羊, a sheep, a symbol of good.

column3: Generous; natural and at ease: 大 "big" plus 方 "manner". Free with money (对朋友很大方) and also relaxed in manner (举止大方). It can also mean tasteful (款式大方). The second syllable is neutral in speech: dàfang. The opposite of 小气 "stingy".
column6: Tā duì péngyou hěn dàfang.
column7: She is very generous to her friends.
column9: Generous; natural and at ease: 大 "big" plus 方 "manner". Free with money (對朋友很大方) and also relaxed in manner (舉止大方). It can also mean tasteful (款式大方). The second syllable is neutral in speech: dàfang. The opposite of 小氣 "stingy".

column3: Warm-hearted, eager to help: 热 "warm" plus 心 "heart". Said of someone who readily helps others or takes part: 热心人, 热心帮助. It describes willingness to help, unlike 热情, which is more about warmth in welcome. 热 has 灬 "fire" at the bottom.
column6: Línjūmen dōu hěn rèxīn.
column7: The neighbors are all very helpful.
column9: Warm-hearted, eager to help: 熱 "warm" plus 心 "heart". Said of someone who readily helps others or takes part: 熱心人, 熱心幫助. It describes willingness to help, unlike 熱情, which is more about warmth in welcome. 熱 has 灬 "fire" at the bottom.

column3: Naive, innocent: 天 "heaven, natural" plus 真 "true". Describes a child's pure manner (天真的笑容), or an adult who is too trusting (你太天真了). Good for a child, mildly critical for an adult. The idea is "natural and true, not yet shaped by the world".
column6: Háizi de xiàoróng hěn tiānzhēn.
column7: The child's smile is so innocent.
column9: Naive, innocent: 天 "heaven, natural" plus 真 "true". Describes a child's pure manner (天真的笑容), or an adult who is too trusting (你太天真了). Good for a child, mildly critical for an adult. The idea is "natural and true, not yet shaped by the world".

column3: Naughty, mischievous: 调 "tease" plus 皮 "skin". A child who plays tricks or does not listen: 调皮的孩子, 调皮捣蛋. A mild word, even affectionate. 调 is tiáo here, as in 调皮, not diào in 调查. 皮 shows a hand stripping a hide.
column6: Zhège háizi hěn tiáopí.
column7: This child is very naughty.
column9: Naughty, mischievous: 調 "tease" plus 皮 "skin". A child who plays tricks or does not listen: 調皮的孩子, 調皮搗蛋. A mild word, even affectionate. 調 is tiáo here, as in 調皮, not diào in 調查. 皮 shows a hand stripping a hide.

column3: Careless, thoughtless: 粗 "coarse" plus 心 "heart, mind". A slip made without attention: 粗心大意, 太粗心了, 因为粗心做错题. About not looking closely; its opposite is 细心. 粗 has 米 "grain" and 且, a grain that is not finely milled.
column6: Tā zuò tí zǒngshì hěn cūxīn.
column7: He is always careless when doing the exercises.
column9: Careless, thoughtless: 粗 "coarse" plus 心 "heart, mind". A slip made without attention: 粗心大意, 太粗心了, 因為粗心做錯題. About not looking closely; its opposite is 細心. 粗 has 米 "grain" and 且, a grain that is not finely milled.

column3: Stupid, clumsy, slow: 我太笨了, 笨手笨脚 "clumsy". A blunt word; with a friend it may be teasing, said of a stranger it is rude. It may be about brains or about hands. 笨 has ⺮ "bamboo" over 本; both parts are simple.
column6: Wǒ tài bèn le, yòu zuòcuò le.
column7: I am so stupid; I got it wrong again.
column9: Stupid, clumsy, slow: 我太笨了, 笨手笨腳 "clumsy". A blunt word; with a friend it may be teasing, said of a stranger it is rude. It may be about brains or about hands. 笨 has ⺮ "bamboo" over 本; both parts are simple.

column3: Capable, able: 能 "can" plus 干 "do". A praise for a person who gets things done: 能干的人, 精明能干. Often said of a woman or a worker. Here 干 is gàn "do".
column6: Tā shì ge nénggàn de rén.
column7: She is a capable person.
column9: Capable, able: 能 "can" plus 幹 "do". A praise for a person who gets things done: 能幹的人, 精明能幹. Often said of a woman or a worker. Here 幹 is gàn "do".

column3: Calm, level-headed: 冷 "cool" plus 静 "still". A person who stays composed in a crisis: 保持冷静 "keep calm", 冷静思考 "think calmly". It describes the mind, not the weather. Of a place, "quiet, deserted" is less common.
column6: Yùdào wèntí yào lěngjìng.
column7: When you meet a problem, stay calm.
column9: Calm, level-headed: 冷 "cool" plus 靜 "still". A person who stays composed in a crisis: 保持冷靜 "keep calm", 冷靜思考 "think calmly". It describes the mind, not the weather. Of a place, "quiet, deserted" is less common.

column3: Self-confident, self-confidence: 自 "self" plus 信 "trust". Both as a noun (有自信) and an adjective (他很自信). Positive; for too much of it use 自大 or 骄傲. 自 is a picture of a nose, which people point to when they mean themselves.
column6: Tā duì zìjǐ hěn zìxìn.
column7: He is very confident in himself.
column9: Self-confident, self-confidence: 自 "self" plus 信 "trust". Both as a noun (有自信) and an adjective (他很自信). Positive; for too much of it use 自大 or 驕傲. 自 is a picture of a nose, which people point to when they mean themselves.

column3: Noble, lofty: 高 "high" plus 尚 "esteem". Used of morals, character, aims and acts: 高尚的品德, 高尚的人. Always positive and a little formal. Not about social class or taste; for refined taste use 高雅.
column6: Tā yǒu yī kē gāoshàng de xīn.
column7: He has a noble heart.
column9: Noble, lofty: 高 "high" plus 尚 "esteem". Used of morals, character, aims and acts: 高尚的品德, 高尚的人. Always positive and a little formal. Not about social class or taste; for refined taste use 高雅.

column3: To concentrate: 专 "single" plus 心 "mind". Verb-object, as adverb or verb: 专心学习, 专心听讲, 不专心. Its opposite is 分心. The idea is giving the whole mind to one thing.
column6: Shàngkè yào zhuānxīn tīngjiǎng.
column7: In class you must listen attentively.
column9: To concentrate: 專 "single" plus 心 "mind". Verb-object, as adverb or verb: 專心學習, 專心聽講, 不專心. Its opposite is 分心. The idea is giving the whole mind to one thing.

column3: Simple, pure, naive: 单 "single" plus 纯 "pure". A person's mind or a plain thing: 想法单纯, 单纯的孩子. Also an adverb, "merely": 单纯为了钱 "just for money". 纯 has 纟 "silk" and 屯, pure silk.
column6: Tā de xiǎngfǎ hěn dānchún.
column7: Her way of thinking is very simple.
column9: Simple, pure, naive: 單 "single" plus 純 "pure". A person's mind or a plain thing: 想法單純, 單純的孩子. Also an adverb, "merely": 單純為了錢 "just for money". 純 has 糹 "silk" and 屯, pure silk.

column3: To do one's best: 尽 "exhaust" plus 力 "strength". Verb-object: 尽力而为 "do all one can", 我会尽力. After it comes the thing to do: 尽力帮你. 尽 is read jìn here.
column6: Wǒ huì jìnlì bāng nǐ.
column7: I will do my best to help you.
column9: To do one's best: 盡 "exhaust" plus 力 "strength". Verb-object: 盡力而為 "do all one can", 我會盡力. After it comes the thing to do: 盡力幫你. 盡 is read jìn here.

column3: Silent, taciturn: 沉 "sink" plus 默 "silent". To say nothing, from calm or for lack of words: 保持沉默, 沉默寡言. A person who speaks little, or a silence in a conversation. 沉 has 氵 and 冗; 默 has 黑 "black" and 犬 "dog".
column6: Tā chénmò le hěn jiǔ.
column7: He stayed silent for a long time.
column9: Silent, taciturn: 沉 "sink" plus 默 "silent". To say nothing, from calm or for lack of words: 保持沉默, 沉默寡言. A person who speaks little, or a silence in a conversation. 沉 has 氵 and 冗; 默 has 黑 "black" and 犬 "dog".

column3: Silently, quietly: the doubled 默 "silent". An adverb before the verb: 默默地工作, 默默地付出 "give quietly, without seeking credit". Often with 地. It praises someone's quiet, unnoticed effort.
column4: 她默默地帮助了很多人。
column5: 她默默地幫助了很多人。
column6: Tā mòmò de bāngzhù le hěn duō rén.
column7: She quietly helped many people.
column9: Silently, quietly: the doubled 默 "silent". An adverb before the verb: 默默地工作, 默默地付出 "give quietly, without seeking credit". Often with 地. It praises someone's quiet, unnoticed effort.

column3: Dear, beloved: 亲 "close" plus 爱 "love". Always before a noun, as in 亲爱的朋友, 亲爱的妈妈, the usual opening of a letter. Used in the way English uses "dear". In speech 亲爱的 is also an endearment between couples. The apostrophe separates qīn'ài.
column6: Qīn'ài de péngyou, nǐ hǎo!
column7: Dear friend, hello!
column9: Dear, beloved: 親 "close" plus 愛 "love". Always before a noun, as in 親愛的朋友, 親愛的媽媽, the usual opening of a letter. Used in the way English uses "dear". In speech 親愛的 is also an endearment between couples. The apostrophe separates qīn'ài.

column3: Close, intimate: 亲 "close" plus 密 "dense". About a relationship or contact: 亲密的朋友, 关系亲密, 亲密接触. It describes the closeness of two people. 密 has 宀 and 山.
column6: Tāmen shì qīnmì de péngyou.
column7: They are close friends.
column9: Close, intimate: 親 "close" plus 密 "dense". About a relationship or contact: 親密的朋友, 關係親密, 親密接觸. It describes the closeness of two people. 密 has 宀 and 山.

column3: To cherish, to take care of: 爱 "love" plus 护 "protect". Objects are things that need care: 爱护公物, 爱护环境, and also children or animals. In signs and rules: 请爱护花草. 护 has 扌 "hand" and 户, the sound.
column6: Qǐng àihù gōnggòng cáiwù.
column7: Please take care of public property.
column9: To cherish, to take care of: 愛 "love" plus 護 "protect". Objects are things that need care: 愛護公物, 愛護環境, and also children or animals. In signs and rules: 請愛護花草. 護 has 言 "speech" and 蒦, the sound.

column3: Patriotic, to love one's country: 爱 "love" plus 国 "country". Verb-object, but mostly used as an adjective: 爱国精神, 爱国者. In 国, a jade 玉 sits in a border 囗. Formal and common in official talk.
column6: Tā shì yī ge àiguó de rén.
column7: He is a patriotic person.
column9: Patriotic, to love one's country: 愛 "love" plus 國 "country". Verb-object, but mostly used as an adjective: 愛國精神, 愛國者. In 國, 或 sits in a border 囗. Formal and common in official talk.

column3: To be fond of, to like: 喜 "like" plus 爱 "love". The object is a person, an animal or a thing: 喜爱音乐, 深受喜爱. More formal and warmer than 喜欢, and often passive: 受到喜爱 "be loved by". The apostrophe separates xǐ'ài.
column4: 孩子们都喜爱这只小狗。
column5: 孩子們都喜愛這隻小狗。
column6: Háizimen dōu xǐ'ài zhè zhī xiǎogǒu.
column7: The children all love this puppy.
column9: To be fond of, to like: 喜 "like" plus 愛 "love". The object is a person, an animal or a thing: 喜愛音樂, 深受喜愛. More formal and warmer than 喜歡, and often passive: 受到喜愛 "be loved by". The apostrophe separates xǐ'ài.

column3: To break up, to part: 分 "divide" plus 手 "hand". Said of lovers who end a relationship: 他们分手了, 和女朋友分手. Also, more literally, of people who part ways after being together. Verb-object, so 分了手. 分 combines 八 "divide" with 刀 "knife".
column6: Tāmen qùnián fēnshǒu le.
column7: They broke up last year.
column9: To break up, to part: 分 "divide" plus 手 "hand". Said of lovers who end a relationship: 他們分手了, 和女朋友分手. Also, more literally, of people who part ways after being together. Verb-object, so 分了手. 分 combines 八 "divide" with 刀 "knife".

column3: Date, appointment; to meet by arrangement: 约 "arrange" plus 会 "meet". As a noun for a date between two people (一个约会) or an appointment. As a verb: 他们约会了. In mainland usage, rather romantic; for a business appointment use 预约.
column6: Tāmen zhōumò yǒu yī ge yuēhuì.
column7: They have a date at the weekend.
column9: Date, appointment; to meet by arrangement: 約 "arrange" plus 會 "meet". As a noun for a date between two people (一個約會) or an appointment. As a verb: 他們約會了. In mainland usage, rather romantic; for a business appointment use 預約.

column3: To get along with each other: 相 "mutually" plus 处 "dwell". People living or working together: 和同事相处, 相处得很好/不好. Read xiāngchǔ, with 处 as a verb chǔ, not the noun chù. The 得 comes after, to show how it goes.
column6: Wǒ hé tóngshì xiāngchǔ de hěn hǎo.
column7: I get along very well with my colleagues.
column9: To get along with each other: 相 "mutually" plus 處 "dwell". People living or working together: 和同事相處, 相處得很好/不好. Read xiāngchǔ, with 處 as a verb chǔ, not the noun chù. The 得 comes after, to show how it goes.

column3: To gather, to get together: 聚一聚 "get together for a while", 聚在一起 "gather together". For friends and family meeting: 好久不见，聚一聚. The object is people, rarely things. 聚 shows several people 乑 with a hand taking an ear 取 and gives the sense of "together".
column4: 好久不见，我们聚一聚吧。
column5: 好久不見，我們聚一聚吧。
column6: Hǎojiǔ bù jiàn, wǒmen jù yī jù ba.
column7: Long time no see; let's get together.
column9: To gather, to get together: 聚一聚 "get together for a while", 聚在一起 "gather together". For friends and family meeting: 好久不見，聚一聚. The object is people, rarely things. 聚 shows several people 乑 with a hand taking an ear 取 and gives the sense of "together".

column3: Party, get-together: 聚 "gather" plus 会 "meeting". Friends, classmates or a family: 开聚会, 同学聚会 "class reunion", 参加聚会. Both a noun and a verb "to get together". Less formal than 宴会 "banquet".
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen yǒu yī ge jùhuì.
column7: We have a get-together at the weekend.
column9: Party, get-together: 聚 "gather" plus 會 "meeting". Friends, classmates or a family: 開聚會, 同學聚會 "class reunion", 參加聚會. Both a noun and a verb "to get together". Less formal than 宴會 "banquet".

column3: Social contact, to socialize: 交 "associate" plus 际 "between". About being sociable: 交际能力, 社交 is a close word. 很会交际 "good with people". 交际花 is a socialite. 交 shows a person with crossed legs.
column6: Tā hěn huì jiāojì.
column7: He is good at socializing.
column9: Social contact, to socialize: 交 "associate" plus 際 "between". About being sociable: 交際能力, 社交 is a close word. 很會交際 "good with people". 交際花 is a socialite. 交 shows a person with crossed legs.

column3: To visit someone out of concern: 看 "look" plus 望 "gaze". The object is a sick person, an elder or a friend: 看望病人, 看望老人. It implies a caring visit and the visitor is often younger or well. Not for a place or a business visit.
column6: Wǒ qù yīyuàn kànwàng péngyou.
column7: I am going to the hospital to visit a friend.
column9: To visit someone out of concern: 看 "look" plus 望 "gaze". The object is a sick person, an elder or a friend: 看望病人, 看望老人. It implies a caring visit and the visitor is often younger or well. Not for a place or a business visit.

column3: To come to someone's home: 上 "go up to" plus 门 "door". Used for a service that comes to your house: 上门服务, 医生上门. Also "to call on": 上门拜访. In another sense it is "to close a shop". Context shows which; the first is the common one.
column6: Yīshēng shàngmén gěi tā kànbìng.
column7: The doctor came to his home to treat him.
column9: To come to someone's home: 上 "go up to" plus 門 "door". Used for a service that comes to your house: 上門服務, 醫生上門. Also "to call on": 上門拜訪. In another sense it is "to close a shop". Context shows which; the first is the common one.

column3: Thin, for flat things: 薄纸, 薄衣服, 薄被子. It is read báo in speech and bó in written compounds such as 薄弱 "weak". Figuratively, "slight, meagre": 薄利 "small profit". Opposite 厚. Its 艹 top suggests plant material, and 溥 gives the sound.
column6: Zhè běn shū hěn báo.
column7: This book is very thin.
column9: Thin, for flat things: 薄紙, 薄衣服, 薄被子. It is read báo in speech and bó in written compounds such as 薄弱 "weak". Figuratively, "slight, meagre": 薄利 "small profit". Opposite 厚. Its 艹 top suggests plant material, and 溥 gives the sound.

column3: Thick: 厚书, 厚被子, 厚衣服 "heavy clothing", 厚度 "thickness". Also "generous, kind" in 厚道 and 深厚 "deep (of feelings)". Opposite 薄. Used of flat things; a thick rope is 粗, not 厚. The 厂 on the left is a cliff.
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài hòu le.
column7: This garment is too thick.
column9: Thick: 厚書, 厚被子, 厚衣服 "heavy clothing", 厚度 "thickness". Also "generous, kind" in 厚道 and 深厚 "deep (of feelings)". Opposite 薄. Used of flat things; a thick rope is 粗, not 厚. The 厂 on the left is a cliff.

column3: Thick, for long round things: 粗绳子, 粗手指, 粗腿. Also "coarse, rough": 粗心, 粗糙, and a "gruff voice". Opposite 细. For a flat thing that is thick, use 厚. 粗 has 米 "grain" and 且: coarse grain.
column6: Zhè gēn shéngzi hěn cū.
column7: This rope is very thick.
column9: Thick, for long round things: 粗繩子, 粗手指, 粗腿. Also "coarse, rough": 粗心, 粗糙, and a "gruff voice". Opposite 細. For a flat thing that is thick, use 厚. 粗 has 米 "grain" and 且: coarse grain.

column3: Thin, slender, fine: 细绳子, 细雨 "drizzle", 细沙 "fine sand". Also "careful, detailed": 仔细, 细心. Opposite 粗. Use it for thin round things; a thin flat thing is 薄. 细 has 纟 "thread" and 田.
column6: Tā de shǒuzhǐ yòu xì yòu cháng.
column7: Her fingers are slender and long.
column9: Thin, slender, fine: 細繩子, 細雨 "drizzle", 細沙 "fine sand". Also "careful, detailed": 仔細, 細心. Opposite 粗. Use it for thin round things; a thin flat thing is 薄. 細 has 糹 "thread" and 田.

column3: Wide, broad: 宽路, 宽肩膀. Also loose (宽松) and generous or lenient (宽大). Opposite 窄. A measurement: 三米宽. 宽 has 宀 "roof", a wide room.
column6: Zhè tiáo lù hěn kuān.
column7: This road is very wide.
column9: Wide, broad: 寬路, 寬肩膀. Also loose (寬鬆) and generous or lenient (寬大). Opposite 窄. A measurement: 三米寬. 寬 has 宀 "roof", a wide room.

column3: Vast, broad: 宽 "wide" plus 广 "extensive". For land, sea, sky and also a broad mind: 宽广的草原, 心胸宽广. Larger and more literary than 宽. 广 is a lean-to roof 厂 with a dot.
column6: Cǎoyuán fēicháng kuānguǎng.
column7: The grassland is extremely vast.
column9: Vast, broad: 寬 "wide" plus 廣 "extensive". For land, sea, sky and also a broad mind: 寬廣的草原, 心胸寬廣. Larger and more literary than 寬. 廣 is a lean-to roof 厂 with a dot.

column3: Shallow: 浅水, 河很浅. Also pale in color (浅色) and simple (浅显), and "not deep" in a person's experience: 经验浅. Opposite 深. 浅 has 氵 "water" and 戋; it recalls a shallow water body.
column6: Zhè tiáo hé hěn qiǎn.
column7: This river is very shallow.
column9: Shallow: 淺水, 河很淺. Also pale in color (淺色) and simple (淺顯), and "not deep" in a person's experience: 經驗淺. Opposite 深. 淺 has 氵 "water" and 戔; it recalls a shallow water body.

column3: Deep, profound for feelings and foundations: 深 "deep" plus 厚 "thick". 深厚的友谊, 深厚的感情, 深厚的基础. It is used for abstract things, never for water or holes. Both characters are measures of a layer; together they show weight.
column4: 他们之间有深厚的友谊。
column5: 他們之間有深厚的友誼。
column6: Tāmen zhījiān yǒu shēnhòu de yǒuyì.
column7: There is a deep friendship between them.
column9: Deep, profound for feelings and foundations: 深 "deep" plus 厚 "thick". 深厚的友誼, 深厚的感情, 深厚的基礎. It is used for abstract things, never for water or holes. Both characters are measures of a layer; together they show weight.

column3: Round, circle: 圆形, 圆桌, 月亮圆了 "the moon is full". Also 圆 as a unit of money (the written form of 元), and "to round off" in 圆满. The 囗 around the outside is a circle; 员 gives the sound.
column6: Jīnwǎn de yuèliang yòu dà yòu yuán.
column7: The moon tonight is big and round.
column9: Round, circle: 圓形, 圓桌, 月亮圓了 "the moon is full". Also 圓 as a unit of money (the written form of 元), and "to round off" in 圓滿. The 囗 around the outside is a circle; 員 gives the sound.

column3: Huge, enormous: 巨 "huge" plus 大 "big". Used for size and degree, and often before nouns such as 变化, 影响, 压力, 成功: 巨大的变化. Said of abstract things as often as of objects. A strong word, more formal than 很大.
column4: 这个城市发生了巨大的变化。
column5: 這個城市發生了巨大的變化。
column6: Zhège chéngshì fāshēng le jùdà de biànhuà.
column7: Huge changes have taken place in this city.
column9: Huge, enormous: 巨 "huge" plus 大 "big". Used for size and degree, and often before nouns such as 變化, 影響, 壓力, 成功: 巨大的變化. Said of abstract things as often as of objects. A strong word, more formal than 很大.

column3: Large-scale, large: 大 "big" plus 型 "type". It appears before a noun: 大型活动, 大型商场, 大型演出. Used for events, machines, companies. Opposite 小型. It is a modifier only; you do not say 这个很大型.
column6: Zhè shì yī chǎng dàxíng yǎnchū.
column7: This is a large-scale show.
column9: Large-scale, large: 大 "big" plus 型 "type". It appears before a noun: 大型活動, 大型商場, 大型演出. Used for events, machines, companies. Opposite 小型. It is a modifier only; you do not say 這個很大型.

column3: Small-scale, compact: 小 "small" plus 型 "type". Before a noun: 小型公司, 小型汽车, 小型音乐会. Opposite 大型. Unlike 小, it classes something as a size category; a small thing is just 小.
column6: Tā kāi le yī jiā xiǎoxíng gōngsī.
column7: He opened a small company.
column9: Small-scale, compact: 小 "small" plus 型 "type". Before a noun: 小型公司, 小型汽車, 小型音樂會. Opposite 大型. Unlike 小, it classes something as a size category; a small thing is just 小.

column3: New type, new-style: 新 "new" plus 型 "type". Before a noun, for products and ideas: 新型手机, 新型材料, 新型冠状病毒. It says the thing is of a recently developed kind. Opposite 老式.
column6: Zhè shì yī zhǒng xīnxíng shǒujī.
column7: This is a new type of phone.
column9: New type, new-style: 新 "new" plus 型 "type". Before a noun, for products and ideas: 新型手機, 新型材料, 新型冠狀病毒. It says the thing is of a recently developed kind. Opposite 老式.

column3: Type, model, mold, mainly in compounds: 血型 "blood type", 发型 "hairstyle", 脸型 "face shape", 类型 "type". Its 土 "earth" recalls a clay mold; 刑 gives the sound. It is seldom used alone.
column6: Nǐ shì shénme xuèxíng?
column7: What is your blood type?
column9: Type, model, mold, mainly in compounds: 血型 "blood type", 髮型 "hairstyle", 臉型 "face shape", 類型 "type". Its 土 "earth" recalls a clay mold; 刑 gives the sound. It is seldom used alone.

column3: To sink: 沉到水底, 沉下去. Also "heavy" (这个箱子很沉) and "deep" (沉睡 "sleep deeply"), and "to lower" (沉住气 "keep calm"). The sense depends on the context. 氵 "water" with 冗 shows something sinking.
column6: Shítou chén dào le shuǐdǐ.
column7: The stone sank to the bottom of the water.
column9: To sink: 沉到水底, 沉下去. Also "heavy" (這個箱子很沉) and "deep" (沉睡 "sleep deeply"), and "to lower" (沉住氣 "keep calm"). The sense depends on the context. 氵 "water" with 冘 shows something sinking.

column3: Heavy, often of mood or burden: 沉 "sink" plus 重 "heavy". 心情沉重, 沉重的负担 "a heavy burden", 脚步沉重. Not for a box you lift: that is just 重 or 沉. A literary, serious word. 重 here is zhòng.
column6: Tā de xīnqíng hěn chénzhòng.
column7: He feels heavy at heart.
column9: Heavy, often of mood or burden: 沉 "sink" plus 重 "heavy". 心情沉重, 沉重的負擔 "a heavy burden", 腳步沉重. Not for a box you lift: that is just 重 or 沉. A literary, serious word. 重 here is zhòng.

column3: Ruler or a Chinese foot (about a third of a meter): 一尺长, 用尺量. The word is mostly in compounds: 尺子, 尺寸, 卷尺 "tape measure". In traditional systems 尺 is divided into 寸. The character shows a body 尸 with a pacing step.
column6: Tā yòng chǐ huà le yī tiáo xiàn.
column7: He drew a line with a ruler.
column9: Ruler or a Chinese foot (about a third of a meter): 一尺長, 用尺量. The word is mostly in compounds: 尺子, 尺寸, 卷尺 "tape measure". In traditional systems 尺 is divided into 寸. The character shows a body 尸 with a pacing step.

column3: Ruler: 尺 "ruler" plus the suffix 子. The everyday word for the plastic or wooden ruler used at school: 一把尺子, 借尺子. The suffix 子 is neutral (chǐzi). A tape measure is 卷尺.
column6: Qǐng bǎ chǐzi jiè gěi wǒ.
column7: Please lend me your ruler.
column9: Ruler: 尺 "ruler" plus the suffix 子. The everyday word for the plastic or wooden ruler used at school: 一把尺子, 借尺子. The suffix 子 is neutral (chǐzi). A tape measure is 卷尺.

column3: Size, measurements: 尺 plus 寸, two old units. 尺寸 is used for the size of clothes, shoes and furniture: 尺寸合适 "fits right", 量尺寸 "take measurements". Also figuratively "propriety", in spoken use: 有分寸 is the more usual phrase. The second syllable is neutral.
column6: Zhè shuāng xié de chǐcun bù héshì.
column7: The size of these shoes does not fit.
column9: Size, measurements: 尺 plus 寸, two old units. 尺寸 is used for the size of clothes, shoes and furniture: 尺寸合適 "fits right", 量尺寸 "take measurements". Also figuratively "propriety", in spoken use: 有分寸 is the more usual phrase. The second syllable is neutral.

column3: Centimeter: 厘 is a hundredth, 米 is a meter. After a number: 一百八十厘米. Taiwan usually says 公分. Read límǐ.
column4: 他的身高一百八十厘米。
column5: 他的身高一百八十釐米。
column6: Tā de shēngāo yībǎi bāshí límǐ.
column7: He is 180 centimeters tall.
column9: Centimeter: 釐 is a hundredth, 米 is a meter. After a number: 一百八十釐米. Taiwan usually says 公分. Read límǐ.

column3: Millimeter: 毫 is a thousandth, 米 is a meter. After a number: 五毫米. 毫 has 毛 "hair" beneath a top part: the finest hair. Taiwan also says 公厘. In general speech centimeters are used for everyday size.
column4: 这块板的厚度是五毫米。
column5: 這塊板的厚度是五毫米。
column6: Zhè kuài bǎn de hòudù shì wǔ háomǐ.
column7: This board is five millimeters thick.
column9: Millimeter: 毫 is a thousandth, 米 is a meter. After a number: 五毫米. 毫 has 毛 "hair" beneath a top part: the finest hair. Taiwan also says 公釐. In general speech centimeters are used for everyday size.

column3: Milliliter: 毫 "thousandth" plus 升 "liter". After a number: 五百毫升. The drink bottle sizes you see on packages: 500毫升. 升 is the liter; Taiwan also says 公升.
column6: Zhè píng shuǐ yǒu wǔbǎi háoshēng.
column7: This bottle of water holds five hundred milliliters.
column9: Milliliter: 毫 "thousandth" plus 升 "liter". After a number: 五百毫升. The drink bottle sizes you see on packages: 500毫升. 升 is the liter; Taiwan also says 公升.

column3: Square, the second power: 三的平方是九. In area: 平方米 "square meter", 平方公里 "square kilometer". The unit is nearly always 平方米. Opposite 立方 "cube". 平 gives the "level" and 方 the "square".
column6: Sān de píngfāng shì jiǔ.
column7: The square of three is nine.
column9: Square, the second power: 三的平方是九. In area: 平方米 "square meter", 平方公里 "square kilometer". The unit is nearly always 平方米. Opposite 立方 "cube". 平 gives the "level" and 方 the "square".

column3: Average; evenly: 平 "level" plus 均 "even". As verb or adverb: 平均每天, 平均分数. And as "evenly": 平均分配. In a sentence the average comes before the verb: 平均每天睡七个小时. 均 has 土 and 匀.
column4: 他每天平均睡七个小时。
column5: 他每天平均睡七個小時。
column6: Tā měitiān píngjūn shuì qī ge xiǎoshí.
column7: On average he sleeps seven hours a day.
column9: Average; evenly: 平 "level" plus 均 "even". As verb or adverb: 平均每天, 平均分數. And as "evenly": 平均分配. In a sentence the average comes before the verb: 平均每天睡七個小時. 均 has 土 and 勻.

column3: Times, -fold: 两倍 "twice as much", 三倍. After a number, as a measure word: 他的年纪是我的两倍. Note 增加了两倍 vs. 是…的两倍; the second is the safer pattern. 倍 is also "double" as a verb in 加倍.
column6: Tā de niánjì shì wǒ de liǎng bèi.
column7: He is twice my age.
column9: Times, -fold: 兩倍 "twice as much", 三倍. After a number, as a measure word: 他的年紀是我的兩倍. Note 增加了兩倍 vs. 是…的兩倍; the second is the safer pattern. 倍 is also "double" as a verb in 加倍.

column3: Here liáng, "to measure": 量身高, 量体温, 量一量. It is a verb, and the noun "quantity" is liàng, as in 数量. The same character, two reads. The verb often doubles: 量一量. The 旦 over 里 gives the picture of measuring a field.
column6: Qǐng yòng chǐ liáng yi liáng.
column7: Please measure it with a ruler.
column9: Here liáng, "to measure": 量身高, 量體溫, 量一量. It is a verb, and the noun "quantity" is liàng, as in 數量. The same character, two reads. The verb often doubles: 量一量. The 旦 over 里 gives the picture of measuring a field.

column3: Weight: 重 "heavy" plus 量 "amount". The number a scale gives: 重量是十公斤. Compare 体重, which is the weight of a person. 重 is zhòng here, "heavy". 量 is liàng, the "quantity" reading.
column4: 这个箱子的重量是十公斤。
column5: 這個箱子的重量是十公斤。
column6: Zhège xiāngzi de zhòngliàng shì shí gōngjīn.
column7: This box weighs ten kilograms.
column9: Weight: 重 "heavy" plus 量 "amount". The number a scale gives: 重量是十公斤. Compare 體重, which is the weight of a person. 重 is zhòng here, "heavy". 量 is liàng, the "quantity" reading.

column3: To measure, to test: 测体温 "take a temperature", 测一下, 预测 "predict". On its own it is a verb with a tool or a quantity as object. 测 has 氵 "water", from measuring water depth, and 则 for sound.
column6: Qǐng nǐ cè yīxià tǐwēn.
column7: Please take your temperature.
column9: To measure, to test: 測體溫 "take a temperature", 測一下, 預測 "predict". On its own it is a verb with a tool or a quantity as object. 測 has 氵 "water", from measuring water depth, and 則 for sound.

column3: To measure, to survey: 测 "measure" plus 量 "measure". Used for land, height, distance, and for instruments: 测量身高, 测量工具. Here 量 is liáng. Suitable for careful measuring; 量 alone is the everyday word.
column6: Gōngrén zhèngzài cèliáng zhè kuài dì.
column7: The workers are surveying this plot of land.
column9: To measure, to survey: 測 "measure" plus 量 "measure". Used for land, height, distance, and for instruments: 測量身高, 測量工具. Here 量 is liáng. Suitable for careful measuring; 量 alone is the everyday word.

column3: To test; a test: 测 "measure" plus 试 "try". A trial of a person's skill (汉语水平测试) or of a machine or program (测试软件). Also a noun. Less official than 考试, which is a school exam. 试 has 讠 and 式.
column6: Míngtiān yǒu Hànyǔ cèshì.
column7: There is a Chinese test tomorrow.
column9: To test; a test: 測 "measure" plus 試 "try". A trial of a person's skill (漢語水平測試) or of a machine or program (測試軟件). Also a noun. Less official than 考試, which is a school exam. 試 has 言 and 式.

column3: Model, type number: 型 "type" plus 号 "number". The exact model of a product: 手机型号, 什么型号. Used when buying, repairing or ordering. 型 on its own means type; 号 turns it into the specific code.
column6: Zhège shǒujī shì shénme xínghào?
column7: What model is this phone?
column9: Model, type number: 型 "type" plus 號 "number". The exact model of a product: 手機型號, 什麼型號. Used when buying, repairing or ordering. 型 on its own means type; 號 turns it into the specific code.

column3: Extremely: 极了 comes after an adjective: 好极了, 美极了, 累极了. Alone as an adverb before an adjective: 极好, 极大. As a noun, "pole": 北极, 南极. 极了 is a spoken pattern that works with feelings and states.
column6: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng měi jíle.
column7: The scenery here is extremely beautiful.
column9: Extremely: 極了 comes after an adjective: 好極了, 美極了, 累極了. Alone as an adverb before an adjective: 極好, 極大. As a noun, "pole": 北極, 南極. 極了 is a spoken pattern that works with feelings and states.

column3: Extremely: 极 "extreme" plus 其 "that". A formal intensifier that goes before an adjective or verb: 极其重要, 极其困难. Stronger than 很 or 非常, and more written. It does not go after the word, unlike 极了.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì jíqí zhòngyào.
column7: This matter is extremely important.
column9: Extremely: 極 "extreme" plus 其 "that". A formal intensifier that goes before an adjective or verb: 極其重要, 極其困難. Stronger than 很 or 非常, and more written. It does not go after the word, unlike 極了.

column3: Especially, particularly: 格 "standard" plus 外 "beyond". It goes before an adjective and means more than usual for the occasion: 格外高兴, 格外冷. It compares the situation with the ordinary one, so it often follows a time phrase.
column6: Jīntiān de tiānqì géwài hǎo.
column7: The weather today is especially good.
column9: Especially, particularly: 格 "standard" plus 外 "beyond". It goes before an adjective and means more than usual for the occasion: 格外高興, 格外冷. It compares the situation with the ordinary one, so it often follows a time phrase.

column3: Excessive, going too far: 过 "exceed" plus 分 "limit". An adjective for words or acts: 太过分了, 过分的要求 "an excessive demand". Often a criticism: 你太过分了 "you went too far". 分 is fèn here, "limit".
column6: Tā shuō de yǒudiǎn guòfèn.
column7: What he said was a bit much.
column9: Excessive, going too far: 過 "exceed" plus 分 "limit". An adjective for words or acts: 太過分了, 過分的要求 "an excessive demand". Often a criticism: 你太過分了 "you went too far". 分 is fèn here, "limit".

column3: Ample, sufficient; fully: 充 "fill" plus 分 "portion". Before a noun: 充分的准备, 充分的理由. As an adverb: 充分利用 "make full use of". More formal and positive than 很多. 充分 is a good fit with abstract nouns such as 准备 and 理由.
column6: Nǐ yào zuòhǎo chōngfèn de zhǔnbèi.
column7: You must make ample preparation.
column9: Ample, sufficient; fully: 充 "fill" plus 分 "portion". Before a noun: 充分的準備, 充分的理由. As an adverb: 充分利用 "make full use of". More formal and positive than 很多. 充分 is a good fit with abstract nouns such as 準備 and 理由.

column3: Thorough, completely: 彻 "penetrate" plus 底 "bottom". An adjective and adverb: 彻底解决 "solve once and for all", 彻底改变 "change completely". Down to the bottom. It suits cleaning, changes and failures. 底 is dǐ here.
column6: Fángjiān yào chèdǐ dǎsǎo yīxià.
column7: The room needs a thorough cleaning.
column9: Thorough, completely: 徹 "penetrate" plus 底 "bottom". An adjective and adverb: 徹底解決 "solve once and for all", 徹底改變 "change completely". Down to the bottom. It suits cleaning, changes and failures. 底 is dǐ here.

column3: Used in 非…不可 "must, nothing else will do": 他非要去不可 "he insists on going". Also "not", in 非常 "very", 非法 "illegal", and "wrong" in 是非. The sense "insist" is the one to learn here. 非 is two wings pointing opposite ways.
column6: Tā fēi yào qù bùkě.
column7: He insists on going.
column9: Used in 非…不可 "must, nothing else will do": 他非要去不可 "he insists on going". Also "not", in 非常 "very", 非法 "illegal", and "wrong" in 是非. The sense "insist" is the one to learn here. 非 is two wings pointing opposite ways.

column3: Almost, nearly: 几 "few" plus 乎 "particle". It goes before a verb or number, and says something is close to the case: 几乎每天, 几乎没有 "almost none". With a negative it can mean "hardly": 几乎不. Read jīhū, with 几 as jī, not jǐ.
column6: Wǒ jīhū měitiān dōu pǎobù.
column7: I run almost every day.
column9: Almost, nearly: 幾 "few" plus 乎 "particle". It goes before a verb or number, and says something is close to the case: 幾乎每天, 幾乎沒有 "almost none". With a negative it can mean "hardly": 幾乎不. Read jīhū, with 幾 as jī, not jǐ.

column3: Easily, lightly: 轻 "light" plus 易 "easy". It is nearly always negative: 不会轻易放弃 "won't give up easily", 不要轻易相信. The meaning is "casually, without thought". You rarely see it in a positive sentence. 轻 has 车 and a sound part.
column6: Tā bù huì qīngyì fàngqì.
column7: He will not give up easily.
column9: Easily, lightly: 輕 "light" plus 易 "easy". It is nearly always negative: 不會輕易放棄 "won't give up easily", 不要輕易相信. The meaning is "casually, without thought". You rarely see it in a positive sentence. 輕 has 車 and a sound part.

column3: Even, so much so that: 甚 "extreme" plus 至 "reach". It names an extreme example at the end of a list or a rise: 他忙得甚至忘了吃饭. Often with 都 or 也 afterward. Written and spoken. The form 甚至于 is rare.
column6: Tā máng de shènzhì wàng le chīfàn.
column7: He was so busy that he even forgot to eat.
column9: Even, so much so that: 甚 "extreme" plus 至 "reach". It names an extreme example at the end of a list or a rise: 他忙得甚至忘了吃飯. Often with 都 or 也 afterward. Written and spoken. The form 甚至於 is rare.

column3: On the contrary, instead: 反 "opposite" plus 而 "but". It points to a result opposite to what one would expect: 雨没有停，反而更大了. Do not use it merely for contrast between two things; the expectation is turned upside down. The apostrophe marks fǎn'ér.
column6: Yǔ méiyǒu tíng, fǎn'ér gèng dà le.
column7: The rain did not stop; it got even heavier.
column9: On the contrary, instead: 反 "opposite" plus 而 "but". It points to a result opposite to what one would expect: 雨沒有停，反而更大了. Do not use it merely for contrast between two things; the expectation is turned upside down. The apostrophe marks fǎn'ér.

column3: Mostly, for the most part: 大 "big" plus 多 "many". Before a verb or a noun phrase: 大多是…, 大多数人. It states what the majority is: 这里的学生大多是外国人. For "most people", the fuller 大多数 with 人. 多 in the old script shows two pieces of meat.
column4: 这里的学生大多是外国人。
column5: 這裡的學生大多是外國人。
column6: Zhèlǐ de xuésheng dàduō shì wàiguórén.
column7: The students here are mostly foreigners.
column9: Mostly, for the most part: 大 "big" plus 多 "many". Before a verb or a noun phrase: 大多是…, 大多數人. It states what the majority is: 這裡的學生大多是外國人. For "most people", the fuller 大多數 with 人. 多 in the old script shows two pieces of meat.

column3: In total, altogether: 总 "sum" plus 共 "together". Before a number: 总共十个, 总共多少钱. It adds up everything. The word 一共 is the same in meaning and more common in speech. 共 shows two hands holding something.
column6: Wǒmen zǒnggòng yǒu shí ge rén.
column7: There are ten of us in all.
column9: In total, altogether: 總 "sum" plus 共 "together". Before a number: 總共十個, 總共多少錢. It adds up everything. The word 一共 is the same in meaning and more common in speech. 共 shows two hands holding something.

column3: Individual, a few: 个 "single" plus 别 "separate". As an attribute: 个别学生 "a few of the students", 个别情况 "isolated cases". It points to a small number out of many, the exceptions. Also "individually": 个别谈话 "talk one-on-one".
column4: 个别学生没有完成作业。
column5: 個別學生沒有完成作業。
column6: Gèbié xuésheng méiyǒu wánchéng zuòyè.
column7: A few students did not finish the homework.
column9: Individual, a few: 個 "single" plus 別 "separate". As an attribute: 個別學生 "a few of the students", 個別情況 "isolated cases". It points to a small number out of many, the exceptions. Also "individually": 個別談話 "talk one-on-one".

column3: Each, every, all the various: 各 "each" plus 个 "item". Before a noun, with no 的: 各个方面 "every aspect", 各个班. It treats a group as separate members. Also "one by one": 各个击破. 各 shows a foot 夂 and a mouth 口.
column6: Gègè bān dōu cānjiā le bǐsài.
column7: Every class took part in the contest.
column9: Each, every, all the various: 各 "each" plus 個 "item". Before a noun, with no 的: 各個方面 "every aspect", 各個班. It treats a group as separate members. Also "one by one": 各個擊破. 各 shows a foot 夂 and a mouth 口.

column3: The rest, the remainder: 其 "that" plus 余 "remaining". Before a noun with 的, or alone: 其余的人 "the others". 其余 is all that remain after you have named some.
column6: Qíyú de rén dōu huí jiā le.
column7: The rest of the people all went home.
column9: The rest, the remainder: 其 "that" plus 餘 "remaining". Before a noun with 的, or alone: 其餘的人 "the others". 其餘 is all that remain after you have named some.

column3: All alike, without exception: 一 "one" plus 律 "rule". An adverb before the verb: 一律平等 "all equal", 一律免费 "free for all". Used for rules and notices. Here 律 is lǜ, written "lv" in pinyin input.
column6: Xuésheng yīlǜ chuān xiàofú.
column7: All students wear the school uniform without exception.
column9: All alike, without exception: 一 "one" plus 律 "rule". An adverb before the verb: 一律平等 "all equal", 一律免費 "free for all". Used for rules and notices. Here 律 is lǜ, written "lv" in pinyin input.

column3: Single, odd, bill, list: 单数 "odd number", 菜单 "menu", 账单 "bill", 名单 "list". As a verb-object in 买单 "pay the bill". Alone it mostly appears in compounds. Also read Shàn as a surname.
column6: Fúwùyuán, mǎidān!
column7: Waiter, the bill please!
column9: Single, odd, bill, list: 單數 "odd number", 菜單 "menu", 帳單 "bill", 名單 "list". As a verb-object in 買單 "pay the bill". Alone it mostly appears in compounds. Also read Shàn as a surname.

column3: Alone, separately: 单 "single" plus 独 "alone". Before a verb: 单独行动, 单独谈话 "talk in private". It stresses being apart from others, by choice or need. 独 has 犭 "dog" and 虫; a lone animal.
column6: Tā xǐhuan dāndú lǚxíng.
column7: He likes to travel alone.
column9: Alone, separately: 單 "single" plus 獨 "alone". Before a verb: 單獨行動, 單獨談話 "talk in private". It stresses being apart from others, by choice or need. 獨 has 犭 "dog" and 虫; a lone animal.

column3: Alone, by oneself: 独 "alone" plus 自 "self". An adverb before a verb: 独自生活, 独自一人. A written word, with a tone of loneliness or independence. Not about being in a room with no one, but about acting without a companion.
column6: Tā dúzì yī rén qù le Běijīng.
column7: She went to Beijing all by herself.
column9: Alone, by oneself: 獨 "alone" plus 自 "self". An adverb before a verb: 獨自生活, 獨自一人. A written word, with a tone of loneliness or independence. Not about being in a room with no one, but about acting without a companion.

column3: Individual: 个 "single" plus 体 "body". A single member, as opposed to the group: 个体差异 "individual differences". Also in 个体户 "self-employed trader", the original use in China. Mostly written or technical.
column6: Měi ge gètǐ dōu bùtóng.
column7: Every individual is different.
column9: Individual: 個 "single" plus 體 "body". A single member, as opposed to the group: 個體差異 "individual differences". Also in 個體戶 "self-employed trader", the original use in China. Mostly written or technical.

column3: Countless: 无 "without" plus 数 "number". Before a measure word or noun: 无数颗星星, 无数次 "countless times". A figure of speech, not a count. The reading of 数 here is shù ("number"); as a verb "to count" it is shǔ.
column6: Tiān shàng yǒu wúshù kē xīngxing.
column7: There are countless stars in the sky.
column9: Countless: 無 "without" plus 數 "number". Before a measure word or noun: 無數顆星星, 無數次 "countless times". A figure of speech, not a count. The reading of 數 here is shù ("number"); as a verb "to count" it is shǔ.

column3: Unlimited, infinite: 无 "no" plus 限 "limit". Before a noun or as predicate: 无限的可能, 无限大, 无限期. Common in set phrases of feeling too: 无限感激. The opposite is 有限. 限 has 阝 "mound" and 艮; a boundary.
column4: 孩子的想象力是无限的。
column5: 孩子的想像力是無限的。
column6: Háizi de xiǎngxiànglì shì wúxiàn de.
column7: A child's imagination is boundless.
column9: Unlimited, infinite: 無 "no" plus 限 "limit". Before a noun or as predicate: 無限的可能, 無限大, 無限期. Common in set phrases of feeling too: 無限感激. The opposite is 有限. 限 has 阝 "mound" and 艮; a boundary.

column3: Limited: 有 "have" plus 限 "limit". 时间有限, 能力有限, 有限公司 "limited company". It says there is a limit, often a small one. Sometimes politely: 我的能力有限 "my ability is limited". The opposite is 无限.
column6: Wǒ de shíjiān yǒuxiàn.
column7: My time is limited.
column9: Limited: 有 "have" plus 限 "limit". 時間有限, 能力有限, 有限公司 "limited company". It says there is a limit, often a small one. Sometimes politely: 我的能力有限 "my ability is limited". The opposite is 無限.

column3: Diverse, varied: 多 "many" plus 样 "kind". Describes variety: 丰富多样, 多样化 "diversify", 多样性 "diversity". Mostly used with 丰富 or in nouns with 性. It is not used to mean "many kinds of" before a noun; for that use 多种.
column6: Chéngshì de shēnghuó fēngfù duōyàng.
column7: City life is rich and varied.
column9: Diverse, varied: 多 "many" plus 樣 "kind". Describes variety: 豐富多樣, 多樣化 "diversify", 多樣性 "diversity". Mostly used with 豐富 or in nouns with 性. It is not used to mean "many kinds of" before a noun; for that use 多種.

column3: Many kinds of, various: 多 "many" plus 种 "kind". Before a noun: 多种颜色, 多种方式. A stable quantity word. 种 is zhǒng "kind" here, with 禾 "grain"; as "to plant" it is zhòng. It comes before the noun, without 的 for most uses.
column4: 这里有多种颜色可以选择。
column5: 這裡有多種顏色可以選擇。
column6: Zhèlǐ yǒu duōzhǒng yánsè kěyǐ xuǎnzé.
column7: There are various colors to choose from.
column9: Many kinds of, various: 多 "many" plus 種 "kind". Before a noun: 多種顏色, 多種方式. A stable quantity word. 種 is zhǒng "kind" here, with 禾 "grain"; as "to plant" it is zhòng. It comes before the noun, without 的 for most uses.

column3: One of: after the group, with 的: 最大的城市之一 "one of the biggest cities". The 之 links, as 的 would, and 一 is the number. A common pattern: 之一 ends a noun phrase and cannot be moved. In writing and in speech alike.
column4: 北京是中国最大的城市之一。
column5: 北京是中國最大的城市之一。
column6: Běijīng shì Zhōngguó zuì dà de chéngshì zhīyī.
column7: Beijing is one of China's largest cities.
column9: One of: after the group, with 的: 最大的城市之一 "one of the biggest cities". The 之 links, as 的 would, and 一 is the number. A common pattern: 之一 ends a noun phrase and cannot be moved. In writing and in speech alike.

column3: Used in fractions: 三分之一 "one third" (three parts, of which one), 百分之五十 "fifty percent". The denominator comes first, the numerator after 之. Say the bottom number first. 分 is fēn here, "part", and 之 acts like "of".
column6: Sān fēnzhī yī de xuésheng méi lái.
column7: One third of the students did not come.
column9: Used in fractions: 三分之一 "one third" (three parts, of which one), 百分之五十 "fifty percent". The denominator comes first, the numerator after 之. Say the bottom number first. 分 is fēn here, "part", and 之 acts like "of".

column3: Accountant; accounting: 会 "reckon" plus 计 "count". A person (她是会计) or the field (学会计). Note the reading kuàijì, not huìjì. 会 reads kuài only in this word and a few related ones.
column6: Tā shì gōngsī de kuàijì.
column7: She is the company's accountant.
column9: Accountant; accounting: 會 "reckon" plus 計 "count". A person (她是會計) or the field (學會計). Note the reading kuàijì, not huìjì. 會 reads kuài only in this word and a few related ones.

column3: Lawyer: 律 "law" plus 师 "master". The ending 师 names a skilled professional: 老师, 医师, 工程师. 当律师, 请律师 "hire a lawyer". 律 is lǜ.
column6: Tā shì yī míng lǜshī.
column7: He is a lawyer.
column9: Lawyer: 律 "law" plus 師 "master". The ending 師 names a skilled professional: 老師, 醫師, 工程師. 當律師, 請律師 "hire a lawyer". 律 is lǜ.

column3: Secretary: 秘 "secret" plus 书 "writing". Someone who handles letters and schedules for a boss: 秘书长 "secretary-general". 秘 is mì here, as in 秘密.
column4: 秘书把文件放在桌子上。
column5: 秘書把文件放在桌子上。
column6: Mìshū bǎ wénjiàn fàng zài zhuōzi shàng.
column7: The secretary put the document on the table.
column9: Secretary: 祕 "secret" plus 書 "writing". Someone who handles letters and schedules for a boss: 祕書長 "secretary-general". 祕 is mì here, as in 祕密.

column3: To work overtime: 加 "add" plus 班 "shift". Verb-object: 加了班, 加班到很晚. 经常加班 "often work late". A big part of working life in China. 加 is 力 "strength" plus 口 "mouth": add something on.
column6: Wǒ jīnwǎn yào jiābān.
column7: I have to work overtime tonight.
column9: To work overtime: 加 "add" plus 班 "shift". Verb-object: 加了班, 加班到很晚. 經常加班 "often work late". A big part of working life in China. 加 is 力 "strength" plus 口 "mouth": add something on.

column3: To handle matters, to run errands: 办 "handle" plus 事 "affair". Verb-object: 办了事, 办事处 "office". Often an official errand: 去银行办事. In a different sense, "to work": 办事认真 "works conscientiously".
column6: Tā zài yínháng bànshì.
column7: He is at the bank taking care of some business.
column9: To handle matters, to run errands: 辦 "handle" plus 事 "affair". Verb-object: 辦了事, 辦事處 "office". Often an official errand: 去銀行辦事. In a different sense, "to work": 辦事認真 "works conscientiously".

column3: To hold a post, to serve as: 担 "bear" plus 任 "duty". The post comes after: 担任班长, 担任经理 "work as manager". For an official role or position; 做 is the plain word. 担 is dān here, "take on".
column6: Tā dānrèn bānzhǎng.
column7: He serves as the class monitor.
column9: To hold a post, to serve as: 擔 "bear" plus 任 "duty". The post comes after: 擔任班長, 擔任經理 "work as manager". For an official role or position; 做 is the plain word. 擔 is dān here, "take on".

column3: Pay and conditions, treatment: 待 "treat" plus 遇 "meet". Used for salary and benefits (待遇很好) and also for how someone is treated (受到不同的待遇). In job ads, "待遇面议" means pay is negotiated. 遇 has 辶 "walk".
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī de dàiyù hěn hǎo.
column7: This company has good pay and benefits.
column9: Pay and conditions, treatment: 待 "treat" plus 遇 "meet". Used for salary and benefits (待遇很好) and also for how someone is treated (受到不同的待遇). In job ads, "待遇面議" means pay is negotiated. 遇 has 辶 "walk".

column3: Unemployed; to lose one's job: 失 "lose" plus 业 "work". Verb-object: 失了业, 失业率 "unemployment rate". The cause of being out of work, not just a lack of job; for someone who has a long break, 待业 is used.
column6: Tā qùnián shīyè le.
column7: He lost his job last year.
column9: Unemployed; to lose one's job: 失 "lose" plus 業 "work". Verb-object: 失了業, 失業率 "unemployment rate". The cause of being out of work, not just a lack of job; for someone who has a long break, 待業 is used.

column3: Spare-time, amateur: 业 "work" plus 余 "remaining". Outside working hours: 业余爱好 "hobby", 业余时间. Also "amateur" as opposed to a professional: 业余选手. The opposite is 专业.
column6: Tā de yèyú àihào shì huàhuà.
column7: His hobby is painting.
column9: Spare-time, amateur: 業 "work" plus 餘 "remaining". Outside working hours: 業餘愛好 "hobby", 業餘時間. Also "amateur" as opposed to a professional: 業餘選手. The opposite is 專業.

column3: Trade, industry, line of work: 行 "line" plus 业 "business". Used for a whole field: 教育行业, 服务行业, 哪个行业. The first syllable is háng, not xíng. 行 shows two steps, a crossroad, and háng is "row".
column6: Tā zài jiàoyù hángyè gōngzuò.
column7: He works in the education industry.
column9: Trade, industry, line of work: 行 "line" plus 業 "business". Used for a whole field: 教育行業, 服務行業, 哪個行業. The first syllable is háng, not xíng. 行 shows two steps, a crossroad, and háng is "row".

column3: Identity, status: 身 "person" plus 份 "portion". Who one is: 身份证 "ID card", 他的身份是老师 "he is a teacher". Also capacity: 以老师的身份 "as a teacher". Taiwan writes 身分 more often. Read shēnfèn.
column6: Tā de shēnfèn shì lǎoshī.
column7: He is a teacher by profession.
column9: Identity, status: 身 "person" plus 份 "portion". Who one is: 身份證 "ID card", 他的身份是老師 "he is a teacher". Also capacity: 以老師的身份 "as a teacher". Taiwan writes 身分 more often. Read shēnfèn.

column3: Position, status: 地 "place" plus 位 "rank". Social, political or economic standing: 社会地位, 地位高. Also the importance of something: 重要的地位. 位 combines 亻 and 立, a person standing in place.
column6: Nǚxìng de dìwèi yuè lái yuè gāo.
column7: Women's status is getting higher and higher.
column9: Position, status: 地 "place" plus 位 "rank". Social, political or economic standing: 社會地位, 地位高. Also the importance of something: 重要的地位. 位 combines 亻 and 立, a person standing in place.

column3: Sales clerk: 售 "sell" plus 货 "goods" plus 员 "person". Someone who sells things in a shop. 售 shows a bird 隹 and 口. 员 ends titles of people: 服务员, 运动员. In everyday speech, 营业员 and 店员 are close.
column6: Shòuhuòyuán zài zhěnglǐ huòjià.
column7: The sales clerk is arranging the shelves.
column9: Sales clerk: 售 "sell" plus 貨 "goods" plus 員 "person". Someone who sells things in a shop. 售 shows a bird 隹 and 口. 員 ends titles of people: 服務員, 運動員. In everyday speech, 營業員 and 店員 are close.

column3: Model (fashion): a loanword from English "model", with 儿 ending: mótèr. 当模特儿 "work as a model". The 儿 ending is northern; Taiwan says 模特儿 and the last syllable is neutral. Without the 儿, 模特 is the same word.
column6: Tā xiǎng dāng mótèr.
column7: She wants to be a model.
column9: Model (fashion): a loanword from English "model", with 兒 ending: mótèr. 當模特兒 "work as a model". The 兒 ending is northern; Taiwan says 模特兒 and the last syllable is neutral. Without the 兒, 模特 is the same word.

column3: Business card: 名 "name" plus 片 "card". 递名片 "hand over a card", 交换名片. In business, it is given and received with two hands. 名 shows a mouth 口 under the evening moon 夕: calling one's name in the dark.
column6: Zhè shì wǒ de míngpiàn.
column7: This is my business card.
column9: Business card: 名 "name" plus 片 "card". 遞名片 "hand over a card", 交換名片. In business, it is given and received with two hands. 名 shows a mouth 口 under the evening moon 夕: calling one's name in the dark.

column3: Résumé, CV: 简 "brief" plus 历 "experience". 写简历, 投简历 "send out a résumé", 发简历. 简 has ⺮ "bamboo" and 间; bamboo slips for brief writing.
column6: Qǐng bǎ nǐ de jiǎnlì fā gěi wǒ.
column7: Please send me your résumé.
column9: Résumé, CV: 簡 "brief" plus 歷 "experience". 寫簡歷, 投簡歷 "send out a résumé", 發簡歷. 簡 has ⺮ "bamboo" and 間; bamboo slips for brief writing.

column3: Interview for a job or school: 面 "face" plus 试 "test". Verb and noun: 参加面试, 面试通过, 我去面试. 面 here is a face in the sense of face to face. Compare 采访, an interview by a reporter.
column6: Míngtiān wǒ yǒu yī ge miànshì.
column7: I have an interview tomorrow.
column9: Interview for a job or school: 面 "face" plus 試 "test". Verb and noun: 參加面試, 面試通過, 我去面試. 面 here is a face in the sense of face to face. Compare 採訪, an interview by a reporter.

column3: To apply for: 申 "state" plus 请 "request". The object is a place, loan, visa or job: 申请签证, 申请大学, 申请表 "application form". Done in writing. 申 started as a picture of lightning.
column6: Wǒ shēnqǐng le yī suǒ dàxué.
column7: I applied to a university.
column9: To apply for: 申 "state" plus 請 "request". The object is a place, loan, visa or job: 申請簽證, 申請大學, 申請表 "application form". Done in writing. 申 started as a picture of lightning.

column3: Training; to train: 培 "cultivate" plus 训 "instruct". Short-term professional courses: 参加培训, 新员工培训. 培 uses 土 "earth", as in tending plants. A person undergoing training is a 受训者.
column6: Gōngsī gěi xīn yuángōng péixùn.
column7: The company trains its new staff.
column9: Training; to train: 培 "cultivate" plus 訓 "instruct". Short-term professional courses: 參加培訓, 新員工培訓. 培 uses 土 "earth", as in tending plants. A person undergoing training is a 受訓者.

column3: Training class, cram school: 培训 "training" plus 班 "class". Extra courses after work or school: 报培训班 "sign up for a course", 英语培训班. The 班 shows a jade cut in two, "to divide" into classes.
column4: 我报了一个英语培训班。
column5: 我報了一個英語培訓班。
column6: Wǒ bào le yī ge Yīngyǔ péixùnbān.
column7: I signed up for an English training class.
column9: Training class, cram school: 培訓 "training" plus 班 "class". Extra courses after work or school: 報培訓班 "sign up for a course", 英語培訓班. The 班 shows a jade cut in two, "to divide" into classes.

column3: To cultivate, to foster: 培 "cultivate" plus 养 "raise". Objects: talents, habits, interests, feelings: 培养兴趣, 培养人才, 培养习惯. A longer, patient process than 培训. Also for raising plants and cells.
column4: 父母要培养孩子的兴趣。
column5: 父母要培養孩子的興趣。
column6: Fùmǔ yào péiyǎng háizi de xìngqù.
column7: Parents should cultivate their children's interests.
column9: To cultivate, to foster: 培 "cultivate" plus 養 "raise". Objects: talents, habits, interests, feelings: 培養興趣, 培養人才, 培養習慣. A longer, patient process than 培訓. Also for raising plants and cells.

column3: To nurture, to breed: 培 "cultivate" plus 育 "bring up". Used for plants and animals (培育新品种 "breed a new variety") and in writing for people (培育人才). More formal than 培养. 育 shows a baby in a womb.
column4: 这所学校培育了很多人才。
column5: 這所學校培育了很多人才。
column6: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào péiyù le hěn duō réncái.
column7: This school has nurtured many talents.
column9: To nurture, to breed: 培 "cultivate" plus 育 "bring up". Used for plants and animals (培育新品種 "breed a new variety") and in writing for people (培育人才). More formal than 培養. 育 shows a baby in a womb.

column3: Opportunity, chance: 机 "occasion" plus 遇 "meet". A fortunate turn of events: 抓住机遇, 难得的机遇. Often paired with 挑战: 机遇与挑战. Compare 机会, which is the everyday "chance"; 机遇 is bigger and rarer.
column6: Zhè shì yī ge nándé de jīyù.
column7: This is a rare opportunity.
column9: Opportunity, chance: 機 "occasion" plus 遇 "meet". A fortunate turn of events: 抓住機遇, 難得的機遇. Often paired with 挑戰: 機遇與挑戰. Compare 機會, which is the everyday "chance"; 機遇 is bigger and rarer.

column3: Future prospects: 前 "ahead" plus 途 "road". About career and life ahead: 前途光明 "a bright future", 没有前途. Applies to a person, a job or a company. 途 has 辶 "walk" and 余 as the sound.
column6: Tā de qiántú yī piàn guāngmíng.
column7: His future is bright.
column9: Future prospects: 前 "ahead" plus 途 "road". About career and life ahead: 前途光明 "a bright future", 沒有前途. Applies to a person, a job or a company. 途 has 辶 "walk" and 余 as the sound.

column3: Skill, technique: 技 "skill" plus 巧 "clever". The method of doing something well: 写作技巧, 技巧高超. The technique is learned and practiced. 技 has 扌 "hand" and 支 as the sound. 巧 is also "skillful".
column6: Xiězuò xūyào yīxiē jìqiǎo.
column7: Writing needs some technique.
